what_you_do: You work on a team led by Teaching Artists. The team makes public art such as murals. You get career development training. Work may also include design, photography, film, screen printing and writing.
deadline_text: The 2026 Application and Interview Weekend has passed. The page says 2027 details will be posted by late 2026.

what_you_do: Sophomores and juniors attend college classes in the morning. The college is Evergreen Valley College. High school classes are in the afternoon.
deadline_text: Recruitment meetings are held in the evening; dates not posted on the page I read.

what_you_do: You get help getting into college and jobs. You also get help with work-based learning, such as internships and apprenticeships. You get mentoring and support services.
deadline_text: Ongoing

what_you_do: Chicago high schoolers join hands-on programs. Areas include arts, communications and leadership, sports, STEM and skilled trades. You earn a stipend. Most programs need an interview, in person or virtual.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 application opened Aug 26 and programs started Sept 28; no closing date stated and spaces are limited. Spring 2027 applications open in January; summer 2027 in April (per the session timeline).

what_you_do: Run hands-on Discovery Station tables about space, astronomy and aeronautics and answer visitors' questions at the Udvar-Hazy Center.
deadline_text: No application window stated; new openings are posted through the year.

what_you_do: You attend a one-week summer leadership session. It is for 11th grade girls. The American Legion Auxiliary runs it. A local Auxiliary Unit chooses and sponsors each delegate. The pages do not describe the daily activities.
deadline_text: 2026 session: June 22-27, 2026. 2027 dates and application deadlines are not posted on the site.

what_you_do: Sign up for volunteer shifts at the food bank warehouse in Oakland. Tasks and times are listed on the volunteer calendar.
deadline_text: No deadline. Pick a shift on the volunteer calendar.

what_you_do: Teens can find volunteer roles at Alameda County Library branches through its Better Impact portal.
deadline_text: Ongoing.

what_you_do: You suggest ideas for library events and projects. You earn 1 service hour per meeting.
deadline_text: Rolling

what_you_do: You can write teen book reviews. Each review is 1 service hour, one a month. Or you can help younger kids with LEGO coding activities.
deadline_text: Rolling

what_you_do: This is a free fair. You meet employers, schools, nonprofits and trade groups. You can explore careers, part-time jobs, internships and training.
deadline_text: The 10th annual fair was Wednesday, April 1, 2026, 1 to 5 pm. No 2027 date is posted.

what_you_do: Help at library branches. You set up for programs, help with computers and clean up. The Teen Advisory Group meets to plan teen library events. It counts toward service hours.
deadline_text: No deadline listed.

what_you_do: Six weeks of paid work with a local employer. You also get an orientation, workshops and a closing ceremony.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Dec 15 and closed Feb 14, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.

what_you_do: Mentor and tutor younger teens after school. Help with events or join the Teen Advisory Board. Unpaid internships are offered. Fields include marketing, graphic design and fundraising. Others are mentoring, IT and social media.
deadline_text: Teen Advisory Board: new high school members are picked each April. Volunteering and internships have no deadline stated.

what_you_do: For three weeks in summer, you work with professional artists. You use a source text. You write and do theater exercises. Then you rehearse and perform an original piece at the Alliance.
deadline_text: The interview and application window runs from January to mid-April each year; the Summer 2026 window is closed. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Walk and socialize shelter dogs, care for cats, help at adoption events, or help wildlife. Teens can earn school service hours. Younger teens and anyone who cannot come in can do at-home projects.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. When read, Wildlife applications were closed and Clinic Support was full. Check back for future opportunities.

what_you_do: Send in a video of a solo with orchestra. The winner plays with the full professional orchestra at the Link Up youth concert and gets a cash prize.
deadline_text: 2026 application closed Sept 25, 2026 at 10 AM. Final round is Nov 7, 2026. Next year dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Help give out more than $100,000 a year in grants to local youth projects, take part in service projects, and go to a statewide summer grantmaking conference.
deadline_text: The page says the new member application is closed until 2027. No dates posted yet.

what_you_do: Prepare materials for library programs, give occasional program support and do shelf reading. Shelving books is done by paid staff.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply any time with the online form, then attend a volunteer orientation.

what_you_do: Work full time in a Michigan Medicine lab. You do your own research project with a mentor. You also take a science writing class and a college prep class. At the end you write a paper and give a talk.
deadline_text: The BioMed Focus 2027 interest form opens Monday, Oct 12, 2026. No closing date is posted.

what_you_do: Help the youth and teen librarians plan and run programs, sign kids up for the Reading Program, and do other tasks all year.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. The group runs year-round.

what_you_do: You sort and repackage donated food in the warehouse. Or you prepare and serve meals at the Community Kitchen. You also clean up there. The kitchen is in downtown Ann Arbor.
deadline_text: Shifts open for sign-up 3 months ahead and fill quickly.

what_you_do: Work on an urban farm. Learn farming, cooking, food justice and how to organize your community. You lead garden and cooking workshops. Summer is 8 weeks. The after-school program runs September to May.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open March 1, 2027. A closing date is not posted.

what_you_do: Help at the science museum and nature center. The page lists staffing the preschool areas, preparing distance learning kits for school groups, and cleaning indoor and outdoor sites. Leslie also has wildlife volunteering.
deadline_text: No dates or deadlines are posted.

what_you_do: After 6 training sessions, you can volunteer on your own. Jobs include cat comforting, dog visiting and shelter cleaning. Others are cat feeding, making enrichment toys and camp counseling. There are also events.
deadline_text: Registration for the November sessions (Nov 2 to 19) opens Mon Oct 19 at 8am; for the December sessions (Nov 30 to Dec 17) it opens Mon Nov 16 at 8am. Sessions are offered monthly and fill quickly.

what_you_do: Learn to make films from working pros. Three weeks cover planning, filming and editing. The camp ends with a red carpet show of your films.
deadline_text: 2026 registration closed Friday, June 19, 2026 at 5 PM. 2027 dates and prices are not posted.

what_you_do: Take a free 4 week course. Explore careers, build job skills, and make a portfolio with a resume and cover letter. Each week you meet a top employer.
deadline_text: Cohorts run throughout the year. No dates are posted on the page.

what_you_do: Drop in after school or join weekly programs. Some are music production, running a concert venue, game design, and first job and college planning. Teens can also start their own project.
deadline_text: School year 2026-27 programs run weekdays. Drop-in is Monday to Friday, 2 to 6 PM. No deadline is posted.

what_you_do: One week of workshops. Topics are public speaking, money and credit, art, teamwork, and help in your community. Youth help plan and run it.
deadline_text: Dates are not posted. The page says it is offered twice a year.

what_you_do: Take the American Red Cross lifeguard course (lifeguarding, first aid, CPR and AED). If you are hired at one of the city's pools, the $200 course fee is refunded. The city also hires seasonal staff at pools, golf courses and canoe liveries.
deadline_text: Registration for the course opens Jan 21, 2027. Session 1 starts Friday, April 16, 2027 (Friday 5 to 10 p.m., then Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.). Registration closes 7 days before the course starts. Seasonal job postings for 2027 are not up yet.

what_you_do: Sign up for park projects such as the Huron River cleanup, Trash Trailblazers, Breeding Bird Survey, Adopt-a-Park and playground maintenance. Groups of 5 to 30 can request a project.
deadline_text: No deadline. Event dates are on the online volunteer calendar.

what_you_do: High school students work with Peace staff and interns as counselors at Summer Day Camp. Rising 9th graders can join as Counselors in Training.
deadline_text: Dates and application steps are not posted on the page.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the summer festival's Top of the Park site. Teen roles include the Welcome Team and Zero Waste Champions. Others are Donation Ambassadors and Merch Mavens. Each shift you finish earns perks. One perk is access to special hospitality areas.
deadline_text: The page says sign-up opens April 1 (for the 2026 season). Festival dates are not on this page. 2027 sign-up is not posted yet.

what_you_do: You get weekly professional development. You get an adult mentor. If you are selected, you get a paid 10 week summer internship with a local employer.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 15 and were due Mar 22, 2026; internship period June 15 to Aug 21, 2026. The site says 2027 applications open in mid-January and are usually open late January to late March. 2027 closing date is not posted.

what_you_do: High school students volunteer in the hospital. They help improve the patient experience. They get a first look at working in health care.
deadline_text: No application dates posted. The 2026 Ann Arbor summer teen orientation was June 24, 2026, 11am to 4pm; no later orientation is listed.

what_you_do: Talk about problems that affect teens. Learn about your community. Suggest changes and new programs to the county leaders.
deadline_text: Application timeline not posted. The page says to contact Britt Baron at britt@neutral-zone.org.

what_you_do: Take career classes while in high school. Your school may offer health science, car repair, cooking, computer safety, hair and skin care, welding, drones and more.
deadline_text: Not posted. The 2026-27 program list is on the page.

what_you_do: Take real college classes at WCC while you are still in high school or homeschooled. Classes can count toward the Michigan Transfer Agreement or a WCC certificate.
deadline_text: No single deadline posted. Check the academic dates link on the page.

what_you_do: Take high school and college classes at the same time at Washtenaw Community College. You finish with a diploma. You also get a two year degree or a job certificate.
deadline_text: Admissions begins Dec 1, 2026. Online application closes Feb 26, 2027. Letters go out Mar 19, 2027. Lottery Mar 26 if needed. Confirm by Apr 9, 2027.

what_you_do: Join service-learning projects with the Youth Volunteer Corps. Or volunteer as a youth helper. You can help in swim lessons, day camps or the Y on the Fly sports program.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply any time with the volunteer application.

what_you_do: Help with kids STEAM programs, the garden, and games like Pokemon cards and chess. You attend a one-hour training first.
deadline_text: The page says the application for 2027 summer volunteers opens in late April.

what_you_do: Teen Advisory Group members plan teen events. They lead them, write grants and talk to youth groups. Other roles are event helper and teen librarian aide (waitlist). Grades 10 to 12 can start their own project.
deadline_text: No deadlines are listed. All Teen Librarian Assistant spots were filled, so the form puts you on a waitlist.

what_you_do: Talk with aquarium guests about ocean life and conservation at touch pools and education carts. You get trained, then work one set day a week.
deadline_text: 2026 windows: Summer applications Mar 1 to Apr 15; Fall applications Jun 20 to Aug 5. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: This is year-round workforce training and education for youth. It serves seven metro Atlanta counties. A contracted provider runs it in each county.
deadline_text: Year-round. No application dates are posted.

what_you_do: You get free tutoring and academic advising. You get help with college applications and financial aid. You go on campus visits. You do career exploration. The program has monthly Saturday Academies. It also has a required summer part.
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.

what_you_do: Free help finding a first job. You get a resume template and a 1-on-1 resume review. You also get interview practice videos and a mock interview. A Teen Job Board lists local openings.
deadline_text: No deadline. Use any time.

what_you_do: Summer Volunteer Squad: teens help at the library over the summer. The Middle School Volunteer Panel meets once a month in the school year. It does service projects and plans programs.
deadline_text: Summer volunteer applications closed on April 30, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.

what_you_do: Spend two weeks with Parks and Recreation staff. You try jobs like park ranger, nature guide, event planner, carpenter and preschool teacher.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened early March and closed May 10, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.

what_you_do: Help camp staff run activities at county camps: field trips, arts and crafts, sports, special events and games.
deadline_text: 2026: registration opened Feb 18 and closed when full. New volunteer interview was April 22 and training June 3, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: A teen group named by the County Board and School Board. Members talk about youth issues and make advice for leaders. They work in one of four teams: drug and alcohol prevention, healthy relationships, peer to peer, or volunteering and internships.
deadline_text: No application dates posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the county hospital on one weekly shift. You give at least 100 hours of service.
deadline_text: No dates posted. Apply any time.

what_you_do: Help the teaching artists in the Armory's kids' Studio classes. You help with set up and clean up, and you help during class each session.
deadline_text: No dates or deadline listed.

what_you_do: Take one-week studio classes in drawing, painting, filmmaking, photography, fashion design, creative writing and more, and build a portfolio.
deadline_text: The page shows the 2026 course schedule. 2027 dates and registration are not posted.

what_you_do: Help patients and staff in a hospital department. Students can see different parts of healthcare before picking a major or career.
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply any time.

what_you_do: Help patients and staff in a hospital department. Students can see different parts of healthcare before picking a major or career.
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply any time.

what_you_do: Students Promoting Environmental Awareness and Knowledge: staff carts around the Garden and talk with visitors about plants and sustainability for short conversations.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: info sessions Jan 13 and Feb 10, application and recommendation due March 1, 2026, group interviews March 21 or 28. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Work outdoors and in labs and greenhouses at the Garden, such as plant conservation research, rare plant care or keeping the Edible Garden and Storza Woods. Build college and career skills.
deadline_text: The Garden says to check back in December 2026 for Summer 2027 details.

what_you_do: Stay at your home school and spend part of each day at ACCA. You study a career path such as HVAC, culinary arts, dental science, patient care, graphic design or cybersecurity. Some paths earn college credit.
deadline_text: The FAQ says students can apply online from November to March. Exact dates and year not posted on the page.

what_you_do: Join free teen activities at city recreation centers, such as sneaker and fashion design, music, cooking, sports training, content creating and graphic design. Registered teens can be considered for Parks and Recreation summer jobs.
deadline_text: The catalog says teens must be registered prior to December 31, 2026 to be considered for the Parks and Recreation summer employment program, and that registration is ongoing. That date is a registration cutoff, not a job application. The catalog also says summer 2026 employment registration is closed.

what_you_do: Take a fall mentorship class, then spend about 40 to 60 hours in the spring interning with a professional in a field you like. You finish with a capstone project.
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Mentor meetings usually start in November. Capstone Celebration in April.

what_you_do: Learn job skills in the community while you earn high school credit. Work-based learning connects your class work to real work experience.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page.

what_you_do: Get matched with a summer job, internship or skills-trade program at an Atlanta employer. Spots are competitive. The city does not promise you one.
deadline_text: The 2026 program ran in June and July. Registration was a waiting list when we read the page. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Get matched with summer internships and research chances. The team also helps with networking and career ideas. It helps you write a resume and a cover letter.
deadline_text: No deadline or dates are posted. After you send the interest form, the team says it will reach out as soon as possible.

what_you_do: Speak up for teens at the library. Work with the teen librarians to improve the library and plan programs for local teens.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Meets the 1st Monday of each month at 6 p.m.

what_you_do: Young residents design a climate project and apply for a $1,000 to $5,000 microgrant to carry it out. City staff help with ideas before you apply.
deadline_text: Applications are open August 24 to October 16, 2026.

what_you_do: Serve as a peer juror in Youth Court. It hears cases of teens charged with a first minor offense. The teens get a chance to avoid a record.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Sessions are the third Tuesday of each month at the Aurora Police Department, 1200 Indian Trail Road.

what_you_do: Help dogs and cats find homes. You greet visitors, walk and play with dogs, and help cats and kittens get used to people. You also help at outreach events.
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply any time.

what_you_do: Six-week paid summer internships in City departments and partner sites. One application covers five tracks: Emerging Leaders, Get Ready (STEAM), Automotive/Entrepreneurial, Aviation Department, and the Austin Convention Center (on hold).
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Jan 28 to Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Paid 8 week arts internship in person at the Dougherty Arts Center and the Zilker Hillside Theater. The page calls it a program for high school students.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates are not posted. Join the Dougherty Arts Center mailing list for updates.

what_you_do: Teens help build homes and help the families who will live in them. Ages 16 and 17 can do new home building. Younger teens do jobs like painting flower boxes, building tables or tutoring the kids of these families.
deadline_text: No deadline. Check the volunteer calendar for dates.

what_you_do: Help care for animals, mostly by getting cats and dogs used to people. You also help with outreach projects that work to end pet homelessness in Central Texas.
deadline_text: No deadline. Register any time.

what_you_do: Work at a business or community partner for 6 weeks, about 20 hours a week. Students are placed by their interests and what is open.
deadline_text: The 2026 interest form closed Feb 6, 2026. A banner on the page says 2027 details are coming and the student form opens in December (year not stated, so confirm).

what_you_do: Paid fellows meet each month. They plan community action projects. Projects include a teen magazine, workshops, open mics and a podcast. Fellows also help host library programs for teens.
deadline_text: Foundation page: the next cohort application opens in May 2027. The 2026-27 application ran May 1-31, 2026.

what_you_do: Help library staff with checkout and programs. You help set up and take down programs. You re-shelve books and run teen clubs. You do light clean-up. You usually work with the youth librarians.
deadline_text: Windows each year: fall Jul 1-31, spring Dec 1-31, summer Mar 1-31. The fall window has closed; the next one is spring, Dec 1-31 (the page gives these windows without a year).

what_you_do: This is a paid creative arts internship. Teens make murals, publications, films and events with local artists. Teens also plan programs for other teens. You learn about Latin American and Indigenous cultures.
deadline_text: Applications for the Class of 2027 are closed. The center will announce when applications reopen for the Class of 2028 on Instagram @atxcaminos.

what_you_do: You train as a certified lifeguard. You work at City of Austin pools and aquatic facilities. New and returning guards fill out an application. They also do hiring paperwork before they sign up for training.
deadline_text: Spring 2026 hiring open hours were Mar 31, Apr 16 and Apr 28 (4 to 8 p.m.) at 2818 San Gabriel St. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Help patients and visitors find their way. You also help with wheelchair rides at discharge, restock nurses' stations and keep patients company. Top needs include the gift shop, discharge lounge and info desks.
deadline_text: The page says applications open March 15 and close April 15 at 11:59 pm, once a year. The year is not stated.

what_you_do: Volunteer at a hospital for the summer. After you apply, you send more paperwork. If you are picked, you interview, finish screenings and go to orientation.
deadline_text: The page says applications run March 1 to March 31 and late materials are not accepted. The year is not stated.

what_you_do: Teens do 60 hours of training, then give 40 hours of service at the museum. Thinkery says 208 VolunTeens served 8,880 hours in its last reported year.
deadline_text: Dates and application window are not stated on the page I could read.

what_you_do: The page describes paid youth internships for teens. It does not say what the work involves. Free elementary day camps and a free middle school Food Lab are also listed, but those are not for high schoolers.
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to watch for future opportunities. No dates are posted.

what_you_do: Free work readiness and life skills training, personal guidance, work experience and help earning a credential for low income youth. In school students are served through Climb the Ladder CTX.
deadline_text: No deadline listed. Start any time.

what_you_do: Meet monthly, hear from City staff, plan actions on community issues and talk with City Council members. Members learn Robert's Rules of Order. They also go to monthly service events.
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says 2027 to 2028 applications are expected to open in Spring 2027.

what_you_do: A City of Austin youth development program for ages 17 to 22. The page says the goal is for youth to earn a livable wage.
deadline_text: No application dates are listed.

what_you_do: This is a yearlong paid internship. It is with the City's Urban Forest Program. You help plan community events. You design education materials about trees. You represent the program in your neighborhood.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 cohort were due March 15, 2026. The page says applications open again in January 2027.

what_you_do: Help at a local library branch. Some branches recruit teen Volunteens each spring to help with the Summer @ Your Library program.
deadline_text: Varies by branch. Teen Volunteens are recruited in the spring.

what_you_do: Young people advise the Mayor, City Council and city agencies on policies and services that affect kids, youth and families. Seats are listed by council district.
deadline_text: No application window is posted. Two district seats (2 and 6) were shown as vacant in the member list.

what_you_do: Five-week summer crew that improves city parks, community gardens, urban farms and vacant lots. Once a week the whole group meets for a class on topics from stream ecology to money skills.
deadline_text: The page still says enrollment for 2025 opens in April. No 2027 dates are posted.

what_you_do: Earn service-learning hours with drop-in community projects, by joining a Teen Advisory Board, or by helping younger kids read and do STEM projects as a Buddy.
deadline_text: Be Involved is drop-in with no application. Teen Advisory Board and Buddies dates are not posted on this page.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the science center and help visitors. The page does not list the exact jobs.
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page.

what_you_do: Take art and design studio classes with MICA faculty, plus workshops and artist talks. Earn college credit. Choose a 2-week or 4-week option, living on campus or commuting.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 dates are coming soon. Tuition is due only after acceptance.

what_you_do: Four weeks of college-level math and intro actuarial science classes, plus field trips, professional development sessions and career exploration.
deadline_text: Application dates are not posted. Students hear a final decision by late May.

what_you_do: Spend a summer as a volunteer guide in the Aquarium galleries after a week of training. Talk with guests and learn about marine science careers.
deadline_text: Applications for summer 2027 open in December 2026 (exact day not posted). 2026 interviews were held in late February and early March.

what_you_do: After-school paid internship with outdoor conservation work, weekly college and career sessions, and money and teamwork skills, with a focus on green careers.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the Branches Fall 2026 session are open now. No closing date is shown. The session dates on the FAQ are from 2025.

what_you_do: Plan and run a library program for teens, meet library leaders, explore careers and give feedback on teen services.
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications closed. Members are told by October 16, 2026. The page says to check back in the spring for 2027-28 applications.

what_you_do: Join a short themed series at a Pratt library branch to earn service learning hours and build skills. Fall 2026 theme is sewing.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications have closed. Groups meet Oct 1 to Nov 24, 2026. The next themes and dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Four days on campus learning what teaching is like, with professor-led activities, a visit to the child care center, the planetarium and library. Earn one college credit.
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened in February 2026 and the session ran July 13 to 16. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Two-year program. Year one is five summer weeks learning lab and clinical skills plus school-year research rotations. Year two is a second summer of applied research.
deadline_text: Applications closed for 2026-2027. The next window is not posted.

what_you_do: One-week hands-on summer workshops on the UMBC campus in science, technology, arts and leadership, led by experts and mentors.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 is over. The page says to check back soon for Summer 2027 registration. In 2026 the one-week sessions ran June 22 to July 31.

what_you_do: Take media classes in video, photo, animation or illustration.
deadline_text: Registration is required. If a class is full, you can sign up for the waitlist.

what_you_do: A paid summer program that mixes media arts training with college and career development.
deadline_text: No 2027 dates posted on the pages I read.

what_you_do: Work a summer job at a city, nonprofit or private worksite, with training on money skills and career exploration.
deadline_text: 2027 youth application: January 4 to February 27, 2027. Program runs June 29 to July 30, 2027.

what_you_do: Work at the front of the theater as a greeter, ticket taker or usher. You can also help in the shop or snack bar, or at events at the Vanier Park festival.
deadline_text: Applications are closed until early 2027.

what_you_do: You get a paid summer internship at BART, 10 to 20 hours a week, in person.
deadline_text: 2026 program ran June 22 to July 31, 2026. Direct applications are not accepted. 2027 not posted.

what_you_do: You can follow career pathways at Berkeley High. There are six areas. They are health, public service, arts and media, IT, engineering and building trades. You can earn credit for an internship or work-based learning.
deadline_text: Choose pathway classes during course selection.

what_you_do: After a volunteer orientation, you can help in the thrift shop. You can help at adoption events or in the vet clinic. You can help with foster care or office work.
deadline_text: Rolling. Internships are 18+ only.

what_you_do: Take UC Berkeley summer classes for college credit in a 6 or 8 week session.
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 2 to Mar 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You can volunteer at a Berkeley library. Use the Teen Volunteer Application. Or work as a paid Youth Worker, up to 15 hours a week. Berkeley YouthWorks hires Youth Workers.
deadline_text: Library page says YouthWorks accepts applications in March and October only. YouthWorks lists a Winter 2027 interest form due Oct 30, 2026.

what_you_do: 10 to 15 Bay Area high schoolers are in this council. They plan Teen Night programs. They host original works showcases. They organize advocacy events. They interview artists.
deadline_text: A new group is chosen at the start of each school year. No 2026 to 2027 dates are posted; join the mailing list for news.

what_you_do: You can get a paid, part-time, temporary internship through the City of Berkeley. The Ready to Work workshop series pays a stipend.
deadline_text: Interest form for Winter 2027 is due October 30, 2026. Summer 2027 information is expected February 2027. Fall 2026 is full through November 2026.

what_you_do: If you are a current or former foster youth in Alameda County, you can get coaching. The coaching covers career interests. It also covers resumes and budgeting. You can get help with job connections. You can get help with training or apprenticeships.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No application window is stated on the pages read.

what_you_do: 8 to 10 week hands-on career programs with expert instructors in fields like healthcare, manufacturing, IT, cybersecurity, culinary arts, photography and interior design. Teens get paid, meet local employers and build job skills.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page. Fill out the interest form to hear about the next session.

what_you_do: Keystone Club builds leadership through school help, career prep and community service. Youth of the Year trains teens in public speaking, resume writing and social justice. Then it holds a contest. Winners can get Club scholarships.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Youth of the Year sessions start each January. Applications are processed in the order received.

what_you_do: Club teens who meet the requirements take paid work positions at the Club. The page says these give real work experience and professional development.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page.

what_you_do: You can join workshops in robotics, art and AI for girls ages 7 to 18. Free Code Along videos on YouTube and mentoring chances are also available.
deadline_text: See the events page for current workshops.

what_you_do: Four-day camp with hands-on practice of life-saving skills, CPR training, nursing skills, operating room instruments and many health careers.
deadline_text: 2026 applications were due Apr 3, 2026. Camp ran June 16 to 19, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Help at an old house museum next to Virginia Tech. You could be a tour guide, store cashier or gardener. You could also decorate for the holidays or help at the July camp.
deadline_text: No deadline. Open season April to December.

what_you_do: Help patients and staff. You work the info desk and deliver flowers and mail. You run errands to the lab and imaging. You also help with patient admitting and discharge and move patients in wheelchairs.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Qualified applicants are called for an interview as spots open.

what_you_do: Join a local 4-H club to build leadership, citizenship and life skills. Teens can join the Teens for a Better Tomorrow club. It focuses on leadership, career readiness and community service. Many members serve as camp counselors-in-training.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Clubs fill first come, first served.

what_you_do: Take arts and humanities classes at Radford University for three hours each weekday morning, earn up to 30 college credits, and do internships and mentorships with regional arts groups.
deadline_text: Application dates not posted on the page read. Ask your school counselor.

what_you_do: Spend a week on campus to try STEM. You can try space, chemistry, biology, computers, rocks, math, robots and drones.
deadline_text: No dates or deadline are shown on the page. It links to a 2026 application.

what_you_do: Day camp with engineering design challenges, drone and robotics activities, construction projects, and tours of STEM labs, construction sites and the Virginia Tech campus.
deadline_text: The 2026 camp was postponed to Summer 2027. New dates and application are not posted yet.

what_you_do: Spend a week at a medical school. A surgeon teaches you stitches and knots. You run health care practice drills and use microscopes. You finish with a small group research project.
deadline_text: 2026 registration ran Feb 6 to Mar 6, with acceptances Mar 15 and week commitment due Apr 1. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Spend four days at Virginia Tech with other 4-H teens in competitive and non-competitive events that build life skills and leadership. Teens stay in dorms. This is the state's main yearly 4-H event for teens.
deadline_text: 2026 Congress was June 16 to 19, 2026. The page gives two different 2026 registration windows: March 6 to May 10, 2026, and March 13 to May 15, 2026 on 4-H Online. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Join the county volunteer program. The page does not list specific projects for minors.
deadline_text: No deadline.

what_you_do: Stay three days in college dorms. Try hands-on STEM activities led by university faculty, with demos and tours. No STEM experience is needed. You can pick one of five campuses, including Virginia Tech in Blacksburg.
deadline_text: Applications open December 1 and close February 1 (the page lists this window with 2027 session dates). 2027 sessions: William & Mary June 20 to 23, UVA June 27 to 30, Radford July 18 to 21, Virginia Tech July 21 to 24, Old Dominion July 25 to 28. Acceptance notices go out at the end of April.

what_you_do: Do hands-on cybersecurity activities. Virginia Tech staff and faculty lead them. You also learn about careers in the field. No experience is needed.
deadline_text: 2026 camps: July 6 to 10 in Blacksburg and July 27 to 31 in Arlington, VA. Applications closed March 24, 2026 and decisions were emailed April 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A week of hands-on design work. You build models, draw plans, scan and print in 3D, and hear talks. It ends with a show of your work. Choose day, overnight in the dorms, or online.
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened Dec 1 and closed May 15 or when full. The page says the program is being rebooted; 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: A full week of solving real earth science problems. Study soil, water, earthquakes and volcanoes. Tour labs and design an exhibit for the Museum of Geosciences.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran June 1 to 5. No registration deadline and no 2027 dates posted.

what_you_do: Build real devices like a drone, a video game console or a digital camera. Learn the engineering design process and how to solder.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions ran June 14 to July 3, 2026. 2027 dates and application deadline not posted.

what_you_do: Spend ten days on campus. Learn about business majors like money, sales, hotels and real estate. Work on a team project. Meet teachers, graduates and company partners.
deadline_text: Application deadline not shown on the page. The page shows the 2026 session; the next one for seniors in 2027-28 is not posted.

what_you_do: Join a program for first generation college students. It has a two-week summer engineering program with team design projects and lab work. It also has campus visits each semester. You get help with college applications and financial aid.
deadline_text: The pages link a 2026 summer program and a 2026 application. No 2027 dates are posted.

what_you_do: A weekend mini camp for string players. You play chamber music and new orchestra pieces. You also do a 3D immersive sound project in the university audio lab. You stay in a campus dorm.
deadline_text: 2026 camp was June 12-14, 2026. 2027 dates and registration not posted yet.

what_you_do: Get free help to reach college. You get career ideas, tutoring, study tips, money help, ACT and SAT prep, campus visits and help with applications.
deadline_text: No deadline posted.

what_you_do: Spend two weeks in a Virginia Tech residence hall. You do a computer-aided design tutorial. You learn to work safely in a cleanroom. You also build and test simple microelectronic devices.
deadline_text: The program page is out of date. It posts no dates for the next camp, and the apply page still refers to the 2025 application. Call (540) 231-7411 or use the Email UPWARDS link on the page to ask before you apply.

what_you_do: Help care for shelter animals with a weekly 2-hour shift for at least 6 months. Younger kids can join Book Buddies and read aloud to shelter animals with an adult.
deadline_text: The page (updated September 24, 2026) says the waitlist is open. You join the waitlist now and get the application link later.

what_you_do: Paid summer job caring for young trees in Bloomington parks, mostly Switchyard Park. You water, mulch, prune and dig around root collars, with weekly enrichment sessions.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Monday March 2 to Friday May 8. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A week-long museum art camp for teens. You sketch in the galleries, look closely at artworks, and make drawing, painting and mixed media projects.
deadline_text: The 2026 teen week is full. The page says registration for each camp opens on the museum calendar; 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Help build homes people can afford on build days. You need no experience. Training and tools are provided. You can also work at the ReStore or join the Habitat club at Bloomington High School North or South.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact Habitat to sign up for a build day.

what_you_do: A week-long summer program where you live on campus. You learn acting for the screen. It runs alongside a filmmaking academy for high school students.
deadline_text: 2026 session ran July 20 to 24, 2026. Students were told by April 26, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Six days on the IU campus to study Black American music, from gospel and blues to jazz and hip-hop. You learn from pros and IU teachers. You also learn how to get ready for college.
deadline_text: Camp is June 13 to 18, 2027 on the IU Bloomington campus. The page has an Apply now link but does not state an application deadline.

what_you_do: A week on the IU campus making films. You try filmmaking, script writing, animation, video editing and acting for the camera. Teachers and film guests lead the sessions.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions ran July 6 to 24. The Media School lists 2027 sessions for June and July (various weeks). No deadline stated.

what_you_do: One week living on campus to explore teaching and school counseling careers. Sessions with faculty and current students, plus a look at college life.
deadline_text: Program is July 11 to 17, 2027. The page says applications will open in February 2027. No closing date is posted.

what_you_do: A five-day camp where you build your own video game from start to finish in IU's game design labs. Pick Game Art and Storytelling, 2D, or 3D (Unreal Engine 5). Beginners are welcome.
deadline_text: 2027 session dates are listed as coming soon on the camp page. No deadline stated.

what_you_do: A five day news workshop on the IU campus. Pick one topic for each session, such as social media, sports news, sports broadcasting, photos or yearbook. You learn from pros.
deadline_text: 2027 sessions are July 12 to 16 and July 18 to 22. No deadline stated; registration link is on the page.

what_you_do: A two week camp where you stay on campus. It is for rising seniors. You hear research talks and do hands-on work with IU teachers. You also learn about college plans, money help and scholarships.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates are not posted yet. In 2026, accepted students were told in late April.

what_you_do: A week on the IU campus in a dorm. You hear lectures, join discussions and do hands-on lab work in genetics, evolution, plant science and more, and learn how to prepare for college.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates are not posted yet. In 2026, accepted students were told in late April.

what_you_do: One week in an IU research lab with a faculty mentor. You do a small research project and present it at a poster session at the end.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates are not posted yet. In 2026, accepted students were told in late April.

what_you_do: A week-long debate camp on the IU campus. You pick a lab in public speaking, Public Forum, Lincoln Douglas or Policy debate and work with IU coaches. No experience needed.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran July 5 to 12; deposits were due by May 23 and financial aid forms by May 23 for the first wave. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A free one-day workshop. You learn about journalism jobs and college options from pro journalists and IU students. You try out Media School rooms and tools. You also make a short podcast.
deadline_text: Saturday, Nov. 14 at Franklin Hall on the IU Bloomington campus. The page does not show the year. Nov. 14 is a Saturday in 2026. Registration is required but no closing date is posted.

what_you_do: A 12-week online program for people who write music, of many ages and skill levels. You get private lessons (Track 1) and a weekly group class. It ends with a live play and recording of your new piece by IU student musicians.
deadline_text: Spring 2027 semester: registration and payment close January 11, classes start January 18, concerts April 1 to 16. The page says Spring 2027 registration begins in mid November.

what_you_do: This is one to three weeks of full-day dance training. Jacobs dance faculty teach it. Topics include technique, pointe, variations and conditioning. It ends with a Saturday studio showing. Dorm housing is optional.
deadline_text: Registration for summer 2027 opens mid-December 2026. Prescreen and registration due February 8, 2027; acceptance notice February 19; payment due March 1.

what_you_do: A week of brass group coaching, master classes and topic classes with Jacobs brass faculty. There are also faculty concerts. For trumpet, trombone, bass trombone, horn and tuba.
deadline_text: 2026 registration, placement recording and payment were due May 15, 2026. Youth forms were due May 29, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A week of jazz groups, theory, improvising, history and master classes. There is a student concert on the last Friday. All experience levels are welcome.
deadline_text: 2026 workshop ran June 7 to 13, 2026. Registration, placement recording and payment were due May 8, 2026. Financial aid deadline was April 13, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You live on campus for a week. You rehearse and perform in a full orchestra or concert band with Jacobs faculty. You take sectionals and a master class. You also take one elective, such as conducting or jazz improvisation.
deadline_text: 2026 session June 14-20, 2026: registration and payment due May 8, 2026; financial aid application due April 13, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: A two-week summer program for serious young pianists with lessons and classes from master teachers. It has run for 39 years.
deadline_text: 2026 application, audition and financial aid forms were due March 2, 2026, with acceptance notices March 13. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A one-week saxophone program. You get four one-on-one lessons (classical or jazz), a technique class, master classes and group playing.
deadline_text: 2026 registration, payment and placement recording were due May 15, 2026. Financial aid deadline was April 13, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A four-week summer program for serious young string players. It has weekly student concerts, Summer Festival concerts and a final gala. It began in 1984 and takes up to 60 students from around the world.
deadline_text: 2026 application and audition were due February 9, 2026, with acceptance notices February 20 and tuition due March 2. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: This is a one-day business case competition on the IU Bloomington campus. You can work alone or on a team of four. You hear Kelley faculty lectures. You meet current Kelley students.
deadline_text: 2026 edition: apply by August 28; competition Saturday October 3 (2026). Next dates not posted.

what_you_do: This is a one-day in-person business program. A two-day virtual option is also available. You hear lectures from Kelley faculty. You join a team case competition. You build leadership skills.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 in-person sessions June 25, July 9, July 16, July 30 and a virtual option April 7 and 14. Application opens Jan 4, 2027 and closes Mar 19, 2027.

what_you_do: Work in teams for a week. You design your own cybersecurity projects with tools such as Wireshark and Nmap. This year's camp also looks at artificial intelligence.
deadline_text: 2027 camp: June 2027. No application dates are posted on the page.

what_you_do: Live on the IU campus. Learn to use Python to control systems and robots. Topics include AI, cybersecurity and robot building and competition. You also cover 3D modeling, virtual worlds and smart homes.
deadline_text: 2027 camp: July (dates to be announced). The page says applications open in January 2027.

what_you_do: Three weeks of acting, singing and dance classes and rehearsals with IU faculty and pro artists. The camp ends with public shows of Chicago: Teen Edition. Students also help with the tech side of the show.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran July 5 to 26, 2026. Application review began April 1 and continued until all slots were filled. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A program of several days on the IU campus. O'Neill teachers lead classes on leading, public policy and community work. You meet IU students and learn about majors and careers.
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 1 and decisions went out by March 25. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Qualified local juniors and seniors can take IU Bloomington courses. You earn college credit. You can take them during the school year or in summer. Spots depend on space available.
deadline_text: Applications accepted about three months before to two weeks before each semester starts. No late applications.

what_you_do: This is a free online pre-college program. It has daily lessons. IU faculty give live talks on climate change, biodiversity, environmental justice and more. You do hands-on activities at home.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 cohort will open January 2027. Closing date and program dates not posted.

what_you_do: A one-day visit to IU for high school students. You tour environmental research labs and join a hands-on workshop led by IU faculty.
deadline_text: Student registration opens in fall 2026. The exact date and the event date are not posted on the page.

what_you_do: Join a 4-H club and complete hands-on projects in subjects you choose, with adult volunteers and staff to guide you. There are community clubs and project clubs, and you can attend any club meeting you like.
deadline_text: Enrollment in Indiana 4-H opens every year on Oct 1. The county asks you to be enrolled and have your clubs picked by January 15. The 2026 Monroe County Fair was June 27 to July 5, 2026.

what_you_do: A free site that lists volunteer jobs from 300 or more local nonprofits, plus events and trainings. You make an account and sign up for opportunities.
deadline_text: No deadline. Each opportunity has its own date.

what_you_do: Teens share their enthusiasm with museum visitors. The page lists no birthday party or outreach roles.
deadline_text: Apply any time. Volunteer orientation sessions in 2026 were listed through Tuesday, November 10, 2026 (prior registration required).

what_you_do: Volunteer your time this summer as a WonderCamp High School Intern. The page lists no specific duties.
deadline_text: Applications for summer 2026 are closed. The page says to check back for summer 2027. Dates not posted.

what_you_do: Start with 36 hours of unpaid Foundation Studio training, then get paid to work in an art or design studio such as painting, graphic design, photography, 3D design, animation or video.
deadline_text: School-year applications are rolling, monthly. Interview invitations went out Oct 9, 2026 for the November group. Hiring pauses through December 2026 and resumes January 2027.

what_you_do: Service learning and leadership program for Boston 13 year olds, run during July and August.
deadline_text: 2026 program is full: registration and waitlist closed. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Five weeks of jam sessions, bands and one on one lessons with Berklee teachers on the Boston campus. Students come from many countries.
deadline_text: The page lists a Jan 31 early-pay discount date. The application deadline is not stated on the page read.

what_you_do: Work in a hospital unit such as X-rays, research, supplies or emergency care. Each week you meet hospital staff for tours and talks.
deadline_text: Application season starts in March and slots usually fill by mid-April.

what_you_do: Volunteer one 3 hour shift a week on the hospital campus. You also go to a one hour talk each week.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: BPS students could apply Jan 21; all students Mar 6; it closed Mar 9 after 100 applications. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Teen members get workshops to get ready for jobs. Topics are coding, digital literacy, communication and teamwork. They get help with resumes. They get career coaching. They also get hands-on internships. Fields include healthcare, culinary arts and finance.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.

what_you_do: You help in a library branch. You shelve books and set up displays. You make book lists and write book reviews. You help lead gaming programs. You learn customer service and job skills.
deadline_text: The page says the program runs year-round, in a fall cycle (September to December) and a spring cycle (January to June). No application deadline is posted.

what_you_do: A three week program with no college credit. You pick one subject. In 2026 the choices were psychology, medicine, creative writing and business. You also do activities in Boston.
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open Dec 17, 2026. Close date not posted. The page says to check back Dec 17 for 2027 details.

what_you_do: You take two BU undergraduate courses. You can earn up to 8 college credits in six weeks. You can be a residential or commuter student. You learn alongside BU undergraduates.
deadline_text: Applications open on December 17. The page does not list a final deadline.

what_you_do: Six weeks of science research. Interns work about 40 hours a week on a professor's lab project; Practicum students do group research. Ends with a poster symposium.
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open Dec 17, 2026. Close date not posted.

what_you_do: A two-week pre-college program on the BU campus. Go to morning and afternoon seminars, join campus activities and get a taste of college life.
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open Dec 17, 2026. Close date not posted.

what_you_do: You work a six-week summer job. You work 20 hours a week. Jobs are in a city department or a nonprofit. Examples include camps, libraries, senior centers, arts, STEM and landscaping. You also get college tours and financial literacy sessions.
deadline_text: Information about the 2027 program will be posted in early spring 2027. Hiring paperwork starts in mid-April.

what_you_do: Youth Organizing Program with two Boston sites. The work is with community and municipal partners on violence prevention and youth development. The page does not list the day-to-day tasks for youth organizers.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page has a Boston Youth Job Interest Form.

what_you_do: Go to Saturday squadron meetings of the Civil Air Patrol. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the wing any time.

what_you_do: You learn to plan and run a 30-minute conservation program. It is for elementary school students. Then you work weekend shifts at the zoo. You guide guests and help care for turtles and rabbits.
deadline_text: Applications for the Winter Teen Conservation Outreach Internship are due December 9, 2026 at 5:00 p.m.

what_you_do: You can work in education, ZooCamp, farm animal care, plant care or marketing. You get career training and life-skills training. You also help build community.
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the program page. Check the zoo's Jobs and Volunteering pages or email the Youth Programs Manager.

what_you_do: You can browse and apply for paid jobs. You can also apply for paid career-readiness programs. These are with City of Boston agencies and nonprofits. They run across the city in summer and during the school year.
deadline_text: School-year 2026-27 opportunities are open now and more are added through spring. Summer 2026 applications were rolling and closed; summer 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Three summers at Harvard for public school students. Summer one is on campus with classes and college planning. Summer two is six weeks of career exploration. Summer three is college-level courses at Harvard Summer School, for college credit.
deadline_text: The page does not list application dates.

what_you_do: You take college-credit courses with Harvard faculty. The program runs 4 or 7 weeks in summer 2027. You can take courses on campus, online or as a commuter.
deadline_text: Application opens December 1, 2026. Early application and priority financial aid deadline January 13, 2027. Regular deadline February 10, 2027. Late deadline March 31, 2027.

what_you_do: Year-round program for grades 8 to 12. Join a dance, music or theatre team rooted in Afro-Latin arts, get mentoring and homework help, and train in civic engagement and youth organizing.
deadline_text: No dates or deadline posted on the program page. The site has a Join Jovenes en Accion page.

what_you_do: Join an after school arts group at the ICA. Groups include the Teen Arts Council, which plans teen events. Others are the Photography Collective, Fast Forward and Teen Exhibitions. The ICA says people in out of school time programs get paid.
deadline_text: The page shows the 2026 to 27 schedules but no application dates or deadlines. Ask the ICA whether spots are still open.

what_you_do: You explore health care careers through hands-on activities and mentoring. Then you can hold paid internships during the school year and summer. They are in hospital departments and labs. You get college and career advising.
deadline_text: The page says applications open in the spring and selections are finalized in the summer. The 2026 link was due to appear in spring 2026; no 2027 date is posted. Summer jobs are recruited through the Boston Private Industry Council (PIC).

what_you_do: Youth Councilors speak for Boston youth in city government and lead their own projects. The 2025-26 council's Streets Committee made a guide for residents requesting ramps and sidewalks.
deadline_text: No application dates posted. The page has an Interest Form.

what_you_do: Work with curators and museum staff. You write gallery labels, plan teen events such as the Teen Arts Expo, and promote the museum to other teens. This is a paid career and college readiness program.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 Teen Arts Council are closed. The next cycle's dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Take a free online course first. Then join a four week summer program. The courses are hands-on and project based. Topics include artificial intelligence, autonomy, radar and satellites. In person options are available.
deadline_text: The page says "BWSI 2027 Online Prerequisites are Now Open!" Self registration for the online course is open now. Approvals come in late January, the online course opens February 1, the summer application is sent in March, nominations are accepted through March 31, and the teacher or mentor recommendation is due April 2. The page does not give a final date for the summer application.

what_you_do: One-week summer cryptography workshop from MIT Lincoln Laboratory.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application and teacher recommendation due April 15, 2026. Decisions mid-June. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Two-week summer radar workshop run by MIT Lincoln Laboratory, held at MIT and at Lincoln Lab. Students live in MIT dorms.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications closed March 11, 2026 (10 p.m. ET). Recommendations due March 18. Decisions mid-May. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You take Saturday STEM classes at MIT during the school year. Topics range from robotics to bioengineering. It is a multi-year program with college application guidance. Lunch is free.
deadline_text: The application deadline is not stated on the program pages read. Check the Apply page.

what_you_do: Spend six weeks on the MIT campus taking five math, science and humanities courses, touring labs and companies, and getting college admissions counseling. Room and board are free.
deadline_text: The application deadline is not stated on the pages read. Check the Apply page.

what_you_do: Join a free, year long after school research program. Greater Boston students meet weekly with mentors on the MIT campus to work on unsolved problems in math or bioinformatics.
deadline_text: Applications are due 11:59 p.m. Eastern on November 2, 2026. Letters of recommendation are due November 6, 2026. Decisions come by early January 2027.

what_you_do: Four-week residential summer program at MIT on the Mechanical Engineering track. Housing and food are in MIT dorms. Open to students with little or no engineering experience.
deadline_text: Application opens Oct 16 in SlideRoom (the page says summer 2027 and does not print the year). Deadline Dec 21. Teacher forms due Dec 23, and late forms are accepted until Jan 20 but delay decisions. Decisions by email mid to late March. Admitted students confirm in early April.

what_you_do: Work at the Museum of Science on projects for a department. You learn workplace skills like talking with visitors, working on a team and managing time. The summer program adds weekly workshops on professional skills.
deadline_text: No openings were posted when checked on Oct 9, 2026. The museum says summer internships are usually recruited in February or March and fall ones in June or July, but timing can change. Deadlines are listed in each posting.

what_you_do: Youth volunteer role at the Museum of Science. The page defines the youth group but does not list the tasks. High school groups from community partners can also volunteer.
deadline_text: No deadline. Join the contact list to hear about upcoming volunteer opportunities.

what_you_do: You work as a Visitor Services Assistant or an Aquarium Guide. You greet visitors. You explain exhibits and ocean conservation. You get training in marine science, climate science and public speaking.
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says to check back next March for the summer 2027 application.

what_you_do: Live in a residence hall on or near Northeastern's campus for twelve days. You take a college style program, mostly led by Northeastern faculty. Academic days run from about 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
deadline_text: The page says Summer 2027 applications open in early December. Priority deadline January 15, regular February 28 and late March 15, each at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. The page does not print the year with these three dates. Deposit deadlines are February 18 (priority), April 1 (regular) and April 15 (late), and full tuition is due May 1.

what_you_do: Do hands-on research with Northeastern faculty. Fields are engineering, science and health sciences. You take a seminar series. It is called Introduction to Engineering. You get college and career advice. You visit company and government sites.
deadline_text: Applications open Dec 14, 2026 and close March 1, 2027 at 5 p.m. Teacher recommendations are due March 8 or 9 (the page lists both dates).

what_you_do: Work as a team with park staff to lead summer camp days for children from Boston youth groups. Trips visit park sites and the Boston Harbor Islands.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed April 26, 2026 at 11:59 PM (rolling until then). 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Join a year-round afterschool and summer program. Roles named on the page include Youth Community Organizer, Health Educators en Accion, and environmental and food justice work. Young people lead awareness campaigns and workshops.
deadline_text: The Youth Employment page says to join the school-year program and click to apply. No dates posted.

what_you_do: Boston youth submit project ideas, help shape proposals and vote on how the City spends $1 million in City funds each year.
deadline_text: Now in the project building phase. The next voting cycle date is not posted. Sign up for the newsletter and follow @oyeaboston.

what_you_do: Join a local Club for after school and school break programs. The pages read describe programs for ages 6 to 18 but do not describe a teen only program.
deadline_text: The home page says 2026 after school registration is open. No end date read.

what_you_do: This is a teen internship in library careers. You get training and field trips on library, college and career skills. Then you do hands-on work. You help with programs and welcome visitors. You finish a capstone project. It is about 100 hours total.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application deadline was October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).

what_you_do: This is a teen internship. It covers early literacy and early childhood education. You get training on child growth and reading. You help children's librarians with storytimes and events. You do a creative project. It is about 100 hours.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).

what_you_do: Interns plan, promote and host after-hours library programs for other teens. You learn event planning, budgeting and promotion. You meet weekly as a team. You give teens a voice in library decisions.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).

what_you_do: Teach and tutor middle schoolers in a six-week summer program after 80 hours of training. The site says college and high school students serve as teachers.
deadline_text: Not posted.

what_you_do: Join a local Sea, Army or Air Cadet corps or squadron. It is a national youth program with challenging activities and training. You pick the cadet element that interests you.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register online and the unit staff contact you.

what_you_do: Get personalized one-on-one support to explore and reach your work and education goals. Help includes resumes, interviewing and managing stress. It is a support program, not a paid job.
deadline_text: No dates. Foundry says no referral is needed to use its services.

what_you_do: Start a trade while you are still in high school. Train in Trades means trades classes and one level of technical training. Work in Trades means paid on-the-job training while you attend high school.
deadline_text: No application deadline is stated on the pages read. Talk to your school for dates.

what_you_do: Compete with other students. Pick a trade or tech skill, such as animation or robotics. The site lists contests. They are regional, provincial and national.
deadline_text: Regionals run February to March 2027 in communities around the province, exact dates not posted yet. Provincials: April 14, 2027 at Abbotsford Tradex. Nationals: May 27 and 28, 2027 in Calgary. Registration deadlines are not listed.

what_you_do: Middle school students do hands-on STEAM projects on Saturdays at the zoo and nearby places. They share a final talk. The 2026-27 theme is being a responsible consumer.
deadline_text: Applications open twice a year: September 1 to October 1 and March 1 to April 1. The fall 2026 window has closed. Years for future windows are not printed on the page.

what_you_do: High school students join workshops, classes and public programs at the zoo. They learn public speaking by teaching guests, take STEAM classes and prep for college and careers. Regular participants can apply for scholarships, travel and seasonal zoo jobs.
deadline_text: Applications open twice a year. Fall: September 1 to October 1 (onboarding early to mid November). Spring: March 1 to April 1 (onboarding early to mid May). The fall 2026 window has closed. Years for future windows are not printed on the page.

what_you_do: Officers teach weekly classes and drills. Topics are gun safety, self defense, traffic enforcement, crime scene work, first aid and CPR. You also go on ride-alongs, work city events and join cadet contests.
deadline_text: No deadline is listed.

what_you_do: A free five-day week of hands-on demos and practice scenes. You see patrol work, the drone team, traffic safety, K9 dogs, crime scene work and simulators. There are field trips too.
deadline_text: The page lists July 20 to 24 but does not print a year or a deadline. Treat it as the yearly pattern and check for the next dates.

what_you_do: You welcome visitors. Roles include podium attendant and gallery roamer. Others are school group volunteer and programs and events helper. This is at the state history museum.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the volunteer program are open. No deadline is stated.

what_you_do: Cadets fly, learn to lead, hike, camp and get in shape. This squadron has members aged 12 and older. It welcomes people who like search and rescue, flying in Cessna aircraft and cyber security.
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join any time. Email the squadron to ask about visiting a meeting.

what_you_do: Help patients and visitors at Burnaby Hospital. You might give directions, eat meals with patients, visit them, or help in clinics. Open spots vary by area.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page says some areas may have no openings.

what_you_do: Take Lifesaving Society courses with the City. They are Bronze Medallion, Bronze Cross, First Aid, then pool lifeguard and swim teacher. They prepare you to work at Burnaby pools.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register for courses online or at a pool front desk.

what_you_do: Greet visitors in old time clothes. Help with school programs and special events, work with old objects, or help at camps. The museum is a 10 acre village from the past.
deadline_text: Intakes: February (spring/summer) and September (fall/winter) for costumed interpretation, school programs and events. Camps: February and April. Collections and sewing: ongoing.

what_you_do: You spend a week at Sacramento State in a summer program for students who finished junior year. You run a mock state government. It has been open to all genders since 2023.
deadline_text: 2027 selection dates are not posted. The Key Dates page (year not labeled) shows delegate selection Jan 15 to Apr 1 and all registrations due Apr 1. Posts usually interview late Jan to late March.

what_you_do: Teens in Explorer posts learn law enforcement skills. They can compete at the CHP statewide Explorer competition. It is at the CHP Academy in West Sacramento. Contact CHP to find a post.
deadline_text: No post sign-up dates are stated. The 2026 competition registration opened December 2025 and full payment was due February 23, 2026. Both have passed.

what_you_do: You can use the Apprenticeship Search to find registered apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs near you. The state agency that registers them is the Division of Apprenticeship Standards.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.

what_you_do: Peer mentors and career coaches help with resumes, interview practice and job search. They also run workshops. They can refer you to GED, diploma or job training programs. It is not a job placement program.
deadline_text: No application dates. Contact a YEOP specialist any time.

what_you_do: Get youth job services. Go to your local America's Job Center of California. EDD lists mentoring, school help and skills training. It lists leadership development. Work experience can be paid or unpaid. It has internships, apprenticeships and job shadowing.
deadline_text: No application dates. Visit or contact your local center any time.

what_you_do: You can volunteer or intern at state parks. If you are under 18, you can volunteer with written permission from a parent or guardian.
deadline_text: Rolling.

what_you_do: Paid service and job experience for young people in their own community. Members work through a city or county partner. The state page does not list job duties.
deadline_text: The state page does not say whether applications are open. Each partner city or county runs its own application.

what_you_do: Work Experience Education (WEE) is a school-supervised job that earns class credit. Exploratory WEE is unpaid job sampling and can start at age 12. General and Career Technical WEE are paid jobs that come with a related class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.

what_you_do: You spend summer days on campus. You build skills in engineering, robotics and AI. You build smart robots. No experience is needed.
deadline_text: Page says applications open in January and close in April each year. Exact 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You can join youth clubs and projects in science, agriculture, leadership and community service. Teen leader roles are also available.
deadline_text: Join through a county 4-H program.

what_you_do: This is a school class or after school program. Cadets lead their peers, plan events and serve their community. They learn citizenship, leadership and wellness. Events include drill, summer camp and leadership conferences.
deadline_text: No dates. Enrollment follows your school's schedule.

what_you_do: Join a school business club. It has contests, leadership training and conferences. These include section and state conferences. There is also a national conference.
deadline_text: No join deadline on the page.

what_you_do: You learn agriculture in class. You run a hands-on Supervised Agricultural Experience. It can be a job or a project. You build leadership through events.
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.

what_you_do: You can join a three-year 'school within a school' for grades 10 to 12. It mixes academics with a career focus, business mentors and internships.
deadline_text: The CDE page lists no student application dates. Each school sets its own.

what_you_do: Six weeks in a Caltech research lab. Students work in student-teacher teams under research mentors and give a seminar presentation at the end.
deadline_text: No deadline listed. The page says spots are limited and usually fill by early spring. It mentions summer 2026 with no schedule.

what_you_do: A firefighting camp for young women. Real firefighters are your mentors. Learn to cut people from cars, handle dangerous spills, rope rescue, first aid, fitness and teamwork.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed. 2026 camp was Aug 7 to 9. Next year not posted.

what_you_do: Youth specialists help young job seekers with tutoring, career exploration, entry-level job training and mock interviews.
deadline_text: The page does not state a deadline or enrollment status. Use the Complete an Interest Form button.

what_you_do: Do community service and plan programs and events. You are the teen voice for the town's Recreation Advisory Board.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The next new member information meeting is not yet scheduled.

what_you_do: Live on campus and train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes carpentry, electrical, painting, plumbing and more.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

what_you_do: You spend two weeks on campus. You take college-level classes in an art or design major. You earn college credit. You build a portfolio. You show work in a gallery exhibition.
deadline_text: 2026 session: registration opened Nov 3, 2025, scholarship applications closed April 27, 2026, registration closed May 11, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: If you are a high school student who qualifies, you get a case manager. You get career exploration. You also get paid job training and work experience.
deadline_text: Ongoing

what_you_do: This is a free day camp at CDC headquarters. It lasts five days. Campers work in teams. They act as disease detectives on public health topics. Examples are infectious disease, epidemiology and emergency preparedness.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The page says to check back in January 2027 for 2027 summer program information.

what_you_do: You help at a large hospital. Tasks include scanning and entering data. You welcome new patients and answer phones. You deliver flowers and amenities. Teens do not do research or help with medical procedures.
deadline_text: 2027 sessions: Winter/Spring (Jan 25 to Apr 4) applications Nov 23, 2026; Summer (Jun 21 to Jul 25) applications Mar 29, 2027; Fall (Oct 4 to Dec 12) applications Aug 2, 2027. First come, first served; each application closes when spots fill.

what_you_do: These are tuition-free college classes while you are in high school. You can take single classes at Chabot College or online. You can take college classes at your own high school. You can also attend a summer academy.
deadline_text: Rolling by term.

what_you_do: You spend three years in this STEM and workforce program. You work museum floor shifts explaining science. You join inquiry teams on engineering and tech projects. You can take leadership roles in later years.
deadline_text: Applications open each year from February 1 to March 31. Decisions in early May, orientation early to mid June. The page does not list 2027 dates.

what_you_do: Junior counselors live at a summer camp near Allerton Park and help run camp sessions for youth. All camp staff get a week of paid training first.
deadline_text: The page says applications open in December and stay open until positions are filled. The dates listed on the page are for summer 2026, so 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Join a faculty research team at the Cancer Center at Illinois for the summer. You are paired with another high school student in the same lab. You also do career workshops and get mentoring.
deadline_text: Dates and the deadline are announced with application materials each fall. 2027 dates are not posted on the page.

what_you_do: You volunteer at Carle Foundation Hospital. You can be a high school or college student. About 500 students volunteer each semester.
deadline_text: Applications are due by 5 p.m. on August 29 (fall term), November 15 (spring term) or April 15 (summer term). The page gives no year.

what_you_do: Get career planning and job search help. Get resume and interview practice. Get work experience. These services are for young people at the Champaign County workNet center.
deadline_text: None stated on the page.

what_you_do: Week-long morning or afternoon camps on coding, electronics, game design, digital illustration, textiles, 3D modeling and more.
deadline_text: 2026 registration is closed. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You volunteer as a counselor-in-training. You work at summer day camps. The camps are at Homer Lake and Lake of the Woods forest preserves.
deadline_text: No application dates posted.

what_you_do: A monthly hands-on club for animal lovers. Each meeting has a talk or activity on animal welfare or sheltering, and time with the shelter animals.
deadline_text: Sessions: March to May, June to August, September to November, January to March.

what_you_do: Live in a campus dorm for a week and take a hands-on academy led by university departments. Topics change each year. The 2026 list included digital farming, and breeding and genes.
deadline_text: ISA 2027: registration opens in February 2027 (exact date not posted). The academy list is posted in early January 2027. In 2026, early registration ran Feb 9 to Mar 1 and the deadline was Apr 17.

what_you_do: Take a two-week beginner class in Modern Standard Arabic on campus for 2 college credits. You also join conversation tables, cooking, calligraphy and field trips. You live in a campus dorm.
deadline_text: Tentative application deadline April 11, 2027. Registration deadline April 26, 2027. Final payment May 28, 2027. Dates may change.

what_you_do: One week on campus in a design studio. You learn drawing, model making and design. You also build bridges, tour campus buildings and take a field trip to a famous architecture town.
deadline_text: Registration opens Nov 1, 2026. No due date; it closes when the program is full.

what_you_do: One week, 3 hours a day camps on 3D modeling, 3D printing, Minecraft, generative AI and robot arms in the MakerLab at the Business Instructional Facility.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 camps ran June 1 to July 31 and are over. Summer 2027 details will be announced in early 2027.

what_you_do: Work in a campus lab on a research project with a mentor for six weeks. You also go to weekly talks on how to share science and get ready for college. You show your work at a closing poster event.
deadline_text: The College of Medicine page says applications open in Spring 2027. No deadline is posted.
