what_you_do: Students spend one week at a campus music camp in band, chorus, orchestra, jazz, rock band, musical theatre or black chorus, with university faculty and visiting teachers.
deadline_text: Registration opens in early 2027. Tentative 2027 weeks: June 21 to 26, June 28 to July 3, July 12 to 17.

what_you_do: Volunteers help patients, visitors and caregivers at the hospital. The page does not list the jobs.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Call Volunteer Services to ask if applications are open.

what_you_do: These are seasonal park district jobs. Examples are lifeguard and swim instructor at Sholem Aquatic Center. Others are summer camp staff, Prairie Farm, sports and grounds positions.
deadline_text: No application dates or deadlines listed on the page.

what_you_do: You can volunteer at parks and programs. Examples include special events and Prairie Farm (May to August). Others are Virginia Theatre, sports and summer programs.
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteers register on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal.

what_you_do: You can take Parkland College classes while in high school. You can take them on campus, online or at your high school. You earn college credit. In some cases, you also earn high school credit.
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask the Early College office.

what_you_do: Short career and hobby camps for teens, taught by professional educators and experts. Camps cover areas that can lead to careers.
deadline_text: The page says registration will open February 2027. Dates will be posted soon.

what_you_do: High school juniors and seniors take career classes at Parkland College (such as automotive, nursing assistant, computer programming, construction trades or EMS) and earn high school and college credit. Classes are in early morning.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Admitted students meet in May for summer orientation.

what_you_do: A paid career exploration program at Parkland College. Students explore college and career programs, meet faculty and staff, and make friends.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was Friday, April 24, 2026 at 5 pm. No 2027 dates posted.

what_you_do: Teens learn about police careers through classes and hands-on training, such as building searches, traffic stops and crash investigation, and do community service.
deadline_text: Apply any time. New orientations happen every spring. Applications are kept on file.

what_you_do: You can help with sorting and shelving. You can work bookstore cashier shifts. You can help with storytime. You can help with a summer Club Fred program. Other roles are listed. Training is provided.
deadline_text: No deadline.

what_you_do: These are week-long camps. You do hands-on projects and tour labs. Illinois engineering faculty and students teach you. Areas include aerospace, bioengineering, electronics, AI and quantum.
deadline_text: All 2026 camps are listed as full. 2027 application dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Local high school students work in a campus department on projects, office support, research or event prep. They also attend about 2 to 3 hours of job skills sessions, usually on Fridays.
deadline_text: The page lists 2026 dates, tentatively June 15 to Aug 7, 2026. It does not mention 2027.

what_you_do: You do six weeks of real research in a University of Illinois lab. Topics include neuroscience, AI, physics and bioengineering. You take part in seminars. You give a poster. There is a final symposium.
deadline_text: Applications Closed for Summer 2026.

what_you_do: Unit 4 students are placed with local employers for a six-week summer work experience. The program also supports students during the school year.
deadline_text: The city page does not post 2027 dates. It says YES places students with local employers for six weeks each summer.

what_you_do: Teens 14 to 18 help the library. Jobs include finding books and items, helping with programs, the seed swap, gardening and book sale setup. Some roles, like Teen Open Lab, need an interview.
deadline_text: Apply any time. No deadline is posted.

what_you_do: You help lead summer day camp activities. You assist counselors and campers. You set personal goals. You meet weekly with other CITs.
deadline_text: 2026 applications were due March 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Join Saturday stewardship days in local parks: collect prairie seed, pull invasive plants and clear trash. No experience needed.
deadline_text: No registration. Fall 2026 dates: Oct 3, Oct 17, Nov 7, Nov 21, Dec 5 (2 to 4 pm).

what_you_do: Teen volunteers help library staff set up and break down, and help run programs and events for kids and teens.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Join a Club after school or in summer. The home page says teens hold Keystone Club officer roles at Southwood, take part in Youth of the Year, and Southwood runs UpNext, a work-based learning program.
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time.

what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer shift at the Charlottesville warehouse. You can also pick an offsite food distribution site. Kids and teens volunteer with a parent or guardian.
deadline_text: No deadline. Sign up for shifts on the online volunteer calendar. Group visits must be booked at least one month ahead.

what_you_do: Join a group led by paid C3 interns. It works with high school green clubs and plans climate action in schools and the community.
deadline_text: No dates posted.

what_you_do: Help with community service tasks at the animal shelter and rummage store. Volunteers are part of the shelter's daily work. Tasks depend on the SPCA's needs and your skills.
deadline_text: No deadline. Pick an orientation date on the SPCA's calendar.

what_you_do: Take hands-on career and technical classes in Auto Service Technology, Carpentry, Cosmetology, Culinary Arts, Electricity, Emergency Medical Technician, Fire Science, Nurse Aide and Patient Care Technician, or Veterinary Science.
deadline_text: No enrollment dates are posted on the pages read. Ask your school counselor or CATEC.

what_you_do: These are paid part-time internships at local worksites. You must finish a required CAYIP Academy on workplace skills. A counselor visits your site at least once a week.
deadline_text: The page lists four school-year sessions and one summer session for 2026-27 but gives dates only for Fall 2026 (applications Aug 20-28, 2026, now closed). For reference, the Summer 2025 application window was April 1 to May 1, 2025 (5 pm).

what_you_do: Go to weekly squadron meetings of the Civil Air Patrol. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron any time.

what_you_do: Care for the schoolyard gardens and join talks about food and how it gets to us. It runs eight weeks in the summer, 20 hours a week.
deadline_text: No dates or deadline are posted.

what_you_do: Help at the Habitat Store (ages 12 and up) or on a home construction site (ages 16 and up). High school Habitat clubs and Youth Build Days also have volunteer chances.
deadline_text: No deadline. No youth events were listed when the page was read.

what_you_do: Make your own short film in a one or two week workshop, such as filmmaking, screenwriting, animation or comedy. Workshops run 9am to 3pm.
deadline_text: 2026 workshops listed June 1 to Aug 7. 2027 schedule not posted.

what_you_do: High school students are paired with expert stage designers and stage managers. You get hands-on training in the work behind the scenes at a theater.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The education page looked out of date when read (it said spring 2026 information was coming soon).

what_you_do: Mentor younger campers at a nature camp. Help the staff plan and look back on each day. Build nature and survival skills with the CIT coordinator.
deadline_text: 2026 spots were filled. Priority applications were due Jan 19, 2026, with scholarships rolling after. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Train one on one with a mentor to run a recording session or the sound at a live show. Then do paid internship work at the Center or at local music spots.
deadline_text: No deadline. There is a wait list form.

what_you_do: This is a lifeguard certification class. The city's aquatics staff runs it. You must pass an in-water pretest. You finish online assignments. You attend in-class sessions.
deadline_text: Session dates were not listed on the page; use the Registration & Tickets link.

what_you_do: Learn leadership skills while helping camp counselors and campers all summer. Each week you are paired with a lead counselor. Counselor training runs before camp.
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened Jan 12 and was first come, first served. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Earn college and high school credit at the same time. Take PVCC classes at your high school, on campus or online. Early College students can earn a two year degree or certificate with their diploma.
deadline_text: No deadline on this page. Ask your high school counselor.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the hospital during the summer. The page does not list tasks for junior volunteers.
deadline_text: No dates or deadline are posted on the page.

what_you_do: A free path to college and a career. High school students get paid internships, college and career advice, SAT prep, tutoring and mentors.
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.

what_you_do: Join a summer crew that fixes the Rivanna Trail around Charlottesville. At the end, you do a three day camping and trail job in Shenandoah National Park.
deadline_text: The article gives no dates. Recruitment ran through the city youth internship (CAYIP) school recruitment each spring.

what_you_do: Six days of design and building workshops. You visit an architecture firm and tour a building site. You hear from pros. At the end you show your work.
deadline_text: 2026 final application deadline was April 3 (early deadline Feb 27). 2027 information will be posted Jan 1, 2027.

what_you_do: Take a real UVA summer college class with UVA students. You pick from 1000 or 2000 level Arts and Sciences classes. None need earlier classes.
deadline_text: No deadline or dates were stated on the page read.

what_you_do: Serve as one of 15 student advisors to City Council. Research issues facing youth during the school year, meet monthly and present to City Council at the end of the year.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.

what_you_do: Help camp counselors with groups of campers at Camp Kingfisher. You help run canoe ponds, play games with campers, and spend time with groups in grades K to 5.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 sessions ran May 26 to July 30 with training May 22. Applications are taken until the program is full. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Join a student team that protects the Chattahoochee River. In the school year you do cleanups and talk to peers about the river. In summer, high schoolers can shadow staff in the field and lab.
deadline_text: 2026-27 application closed Monday Sept 21, 2026. Next cycle not posted.

what_you_do: Teens see how the Adler plans guest visits behind the scenes. They learn to lead hands-on science activities and share ideas with staff. Then they run the activities for guests on the museum floor.
deadline_text: Applications for the spring 2027 session open in early 2027. Exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: Teens join Adler researchers to study light pollution in and around Chicago. One long study looks at how light affects trees. Teens also make a science poster and give a talk.
deadline_text: Applications for the spring 2027 session open in early 2027. Exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: A group of 15 teens works with museum staff. They plan programs and tools that make the museum more welcoming and useful for Chicago-area youth. Members meet at the museum and go behind the scenes.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 Teen Council application was open through June 30, 2026. 2027-28 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Interns help with festivals, gallery tours and workshops. They meet museum workers and local artists. They also plan and host creative events for visitors.
deadline_text: Applications open in the spring through After School Matters. Exact 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Rising CPS juniors and seniors take a college-level environmental science class and get a mentor. They do a summer research project. Through the school year they get help with college applications. The job is paid, with school-year stipends.
deadline_text: Page says the application deadline is Tuesday, April 15 (no year shown).

what_you_do: Rising CPS freshmen and sophomores spend four weeks at the Garden. They learn about nature, biology, ecology and environmental justice. They do group projects and show them to family and friends. Students are paid.
deadline_text: Page says the application deadline is Tuesday, April 15 (no year shown).

what_you_do: A four-week program for high school students. You take a freshman-level college class in the arts, media or communications. Your teachers work in those fields. Credits can count if you enroll at Columbia later.
deadline_text: 2026 registration has closed. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Each summer, 15 Chicago-area high school students pick a Field Museum scientist or expert. They do a 5-week research project. They also learn digital media, tech and career skills.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed. The page says to check back in early 2027 for next summer.

what_you_do: Paid summer interns link their neighborhoods with the Burnham Wildlife Corridor. It is a nature area on the south lakefront. Interns work on real problems in the environment and in the community.
deadline_text: Dates and application not posted on the program page.

what_you_do: Teens greet visitors and share science stories. They help young kids in the Crown Family PlayLab and show real specimens at interpretive carts in Stanley Field Hall.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Jan 2026 to Feb 28, 2026. Interviews late March or early April; final notice by May 8. The page says check back in early 2027.

what_you_do: Teens learn screenwriting, editing, camera work, audio and acting. Programs run after school, in school and in summer. Teens also get job skills training.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 programs: Sept 21 to Nov 20, 2026. Registration deadline not stated.

what_you_do: Juniors get 8 weeks of training in business and tech skills. In senior year they work a paid internship at a partner company for about 20 hours a week. The internship lasts a year. They also get college and career coaching.
deadline_text: Students at partner schools apply in fall or winter of junior year and finish the process in spring. Exact 2026-27 dates not posted on the pages read.

what_you_do: A free summer program. Teens train in acting, singing and dancing with professional musical theater artists. They perform in a show at the Goodman.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed; callbacks were Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: A free summer theater program. Teens learn acting, creative writing, improv and physical theater from pros. They create an original show about civic issues.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed; callbacks were Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: CPS students use theater to talk about issues that young people face. They plan and run events by teens for teens. They learn from Goodman artists and staff, and they act as ambassadors for the theater.
deadline_text: Applications for 2025/26 are closed. 2026/27 dates not posted on the page read.

what_you_do: A free program where teens explore careers in science, tech, engineering, arts and math. You do hands-on projects, LEGO engineering challenges and panels with pros and mentors. You can join a 12-week session or drop in.
deadline_text: Registration for the Fall 2026 session has closed. Next session dates not posted.

what_you_do: Students pick a topic that fits the yearly theme and research it like a historian. Then they make a website, show, film, paper or exhibit. Volunteers judge the projects at yearly contests in the Chicago area.
deadline_text: 2027 theme: Innovation in History. Teacher intent form due Dec 1, 2026. Student project registration due Feb 10, 2027; upload due Feb 17, 2027. Regional contest Feb 27, 2027 (grades 9-12). Junior Division (grades 6-8) Mar 6, 2027. National contest June 13-17, 2027.

what_you_do: Teen volunteers help counselors run Conservation Camp for young kids. They set up activities, join in and help make camp fun. They earn service hours and an EcoLeader certificate.
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Each semester, teens study one conservation topic in depth. Then they plan and carry out a project and share it with peers and the public. They build skills in leadership, research, speaking, event planning, promotion and money.
deadline_text: Spring 2026 application opened Jan 20 and was due Feb 1. A fall term also runs. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Interns help run nature play for the zoo's youngest visitors. There is music, art, story time and sensory bins. Interns also help kids and the adults with them find their way around the zoo.
deadline_text: 2026 application opened the week of April 27 on the After School Matters site. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Apprentices work with zoo researchers on a real science question. They learn research methods in the field and on computers. At the end of summer they show their results at a poster session.
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Interns teach zoo guests about animals and conservation. They learn how to share conservation messages. They meet zoo researchers and animal care staff. They finish with a project they present.
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Free events just for teens, led by zoo experts. You can make conservation art, learn to live next to city wildlife like bats and birds, and play a role-playing game.
deadline_text: Events listed for Saturday Oct 31 (Roll for Wildlife, Prism Games, Logan Square) and Saturday Nov 7 (Plants and Prints, Lincoln Park Zoo). The page does not state the year. Register on the page.

what_you_do: Nearly 20 young people are hired for paid 5-week internships. The jobs are at arts groups and creative businesses. Interns also go to Marwen workshops. Topics are resumes, interviews, public speaking and money.
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open in spring 2027. For 2026 they were due April 11, 2026.

what_you_do: Chicago teens meet each week with two lead artists. They spend time in the galleries and at other culture sites. They make art projects and public events, including the yearly teen show called 21Minus.
deadline_text: Applications for TCA open next spring (spring 2027). Exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: Students from 20+ Chicago schools meet with CPS leaders. They gather ideas from peers and do research. Then they write advice on school issues. Past groups spoke to the CPS Board.
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: Youth who live in Chicago or Cook County give advice to the Cook County Board President. They talk about youth justice, safety in the community and holding police responsible. They write advice each year.
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: High school juniors and seniors work at polling places on Election Day. They do the same jobs as adult judges. They help voters, run the machines and close the polls.
deadline_text: Each election cycle. No dates posted on the page.

what_you_do: Fellows work for six weeks in the offices of city, county, state and federal leaders. They also go to weekly workshops on leadership, setting goals and job skills.
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: Teens study the physical, mental and sexual health of Chicago youth. They make action plans. They share ideas with the Chicago Department of Public Health and CPS. They also learn about public health careers.
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: This is a mentoring and job-readiness program for 13 to 15 year olds. Teens help with park programs. Programs include sports, games, nature and arts and crafts. You build leadership, communication and customer service skills.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Teens 16 and up can work in the parks. Jobs include lifeguard and day camp recreation leader. You can also be a special recreation leader. Those camps serve kids and adults with intellectual disabilities. Junior laborers do landscape work.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.

what_you_do: Volunteers greet visitors and walk them to where they need to go. They push wheelchairs, deliver flowers and mail, visit with patients and help with events. After six months you can apply for a role in one department.
deadline_text: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis.

what_you_do: High school students take art and design classes in fall, spring or summer. Examples are figure drawing, animation, fashion and comics. You build work for your portfolio for art school.
deadline_text: Register online for each term. No fixed deadline stated on the pages read.

what_you_do: Intensive 1, 2 or 4-week summer art and design courses at SAIC. Students earn one college credit for each week attended.
deadline_text: Page says registration opens November 1 (year not stated). The 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31. A priority deadline is mentioned but not dated on the page read.

what_you_do: 30 high school students meet every Wednesday to learn how a big theater works. They see plays, join workshops with theater artists, and plan teen nights with the ensemble.
deadline_text: Page says applications are closed. Next dates not posted.

what_you_do: Advanced CPS juniors and seniors take one college class each quarter at the University of Chicago. They sit in class with UChicago students. The classes go on the CPS transcript.
deadline_text: For 2026-27 the application opened June 8, 2026 and closed July 15, 2026. 2027-28 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Students work full time in a University of Chicago cancer research lab for two summers. They also get monthly career workshops, talks and mentors. They present at a research event.
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Nov 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT. In-person interviews Jan 4, 2027.

what_you_do: A two-week online program where high school students work on a cancer genetics project and a patient case study, hear daily faculty talks and build skills. Students get a home lab kit.
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Mar 1, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Interviews in April 2027.

what_you_do: Student volunteers help patients, families and visitors in the hospital. They welcome people and visit with patients. They help families find their way. Roles include Child Life and patient comfort teams.
deadline_text: Fall window ran Aug 25 to Oct 1, 2026 (may close early). Next cycle starts Jan 10, 2027; closing date not posted.

what_you_do: High school students spend 8 weeks in a cancer research lab. They work 35 to 40 hours a week. The lab is at one of five Illinois universities. Students also get career workshops and mentors.
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Jan 11, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. On-campus interviews in February 2027; acceptance notices March 1, 2027.

what_you_do: High school students take college-level courses in person (live on campus or commute) or online. Choices run from short programs to research courses. Examples are lab biology or fieldwork with Field Museum fossil experts.
deadline_text: 2026 deadlines: priority Feb 11, regular Mar 12 (Practicum priority only). 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Teens grow food on urban farms, tend beehives, cook with what they grow, and sell it at farm stands and markets. They build leadership and job skills and explore careers in food and farming.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.

what_you_do: The City runs a summer youth jobs program. It places young people in paid jobs. Partners include the Park District, CPS and City Colleges. Others are the Chicago Housing Authority, the Forest Preserves and Lincoln Park Zoo.
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.

what_you_do: This is a six-week summer program. It has workforce training, financial literacy training and career exploration. It has 120 hours of activities. You make a resume. You sign up for direct deposit.
deadline_text: The 2026 Chicago Youth Works application (which covers 14 to 24 year olds) ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer in a children's hospital over the summer, at least one 3-hour shift a week for eight weeks. Placements are at Arthur M. Blank, Hughes Spalding or Scottish Rite hospitals.
deadline_text: The page says the next chance to apply is February 2027; exact open and close dates are not posted yet.

what_you_do: You can join an Explorer post for teens who want a law enforcement career. You get training and mentoring from CHP officers.
deadline_text: Rolling.

what_you_do: You serve patients and visitors. You support hospital staff. You explore health care careers. You work one 4 hour shift each week.
deadline_text: Three cycles a year: summer apply by April 30, fall by August 30, spring by December 30. The page lists month and day only, no year.

what_you_do: Help at a nature center and wildlife rescue by supporting events, working on the grounds and in the office, and later in animal care. Orientations are held on weekends.
deadline_text: Accepted on a rolling basis. Orientations are on alternating Saturdays and Sundays at 10 a.m. each month.

what_you_do: Help plan the 10x10 Teen Art Expo, a week long exhibition of more than 100 teen artists from the greater Cincinnati region. The team picks the theme that artists use for their 10 by 10 inch pieces and meets monthly.
deadline_text: Volunteer applications for the 2026 to 27 team were due Friday September 4, 2026, with replies by September 11. Next year's dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Join the Clubs' teen Workforce Development programming. You explore careers with local businesses. You also explore careers with universities, trades and the military. You learn about money. You get ready for jobs. Driver's education is part of it too.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Enroll through the Club member portal.

what_you_do: You join monthly workshops with local artists, tour the museum behind the scenes, and plan a CAC-sponsored teen event. You also post on the teen Instagram account.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 enrollment deadline was July 11. The next deadline is not posted.

what_you_do: A one week summer ballet program. You work on ballet skills, pointe and modern dance. You also take classes on avoiding injury, healthy eating and pilates.
deadline_text: Registration opens in January 2027. A closing date is not stated on the page.

what_you_do: You train in singing, dance and acting. Teachers from the conservatory and local pros lead you. Pick a 1 week or 2 week summer session.
deadline_text: Auditions opened Oct 1, 2026. Priority deadline Feb 15, 2027. Final deadline March 1, 2027.

what_you_do: A one week summer program for high school string players. You play in small groups and a string orchestra. You learn from pros in master classes. It ends with a concert.
deadline_text: Auditions opened Oct 1, 2026. Priority deadline Feb 15, 2027. Final deadline March 15, 2027.

what_you_do: A one month summer program. You learn by doing and grow work skills with experts across the hospital. It replaces the earlier paid summer internship.
deadline_text: Online application opens Nov 1 and closes Feb 1, for summer 2027.

what_you_do: You complete tasks under hospital staff supervision. This is in the pediatric setting. You work a 2 to 3 hour shift each week. You build teamwork and leadership skills.
deadline_text: The deadline for the Summer 2026 session has passed. The page says the summer application is usually posted in January, with about two months to finish the packet.

what_you_do: You work on a district team that matches your career goals for 6 to 8 weeks, for example facilities or communications. You shadow staff, do real tasks and tour school sites.
deadline_text: No application dates are given on the page read.

what_you_do: You can work part-time or seasonal jobs at Cincinnati public pools. Lifeguards keep pool users safe. Gate and pool monitors handle customer service. They also watch behavior around the pool.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. A 2026 lifeguard screening registration form is linked.

what_you_do: You work a summer job with City departments or nonprofit partners. Examples include recreation centers, pools, parks, fire and police cadets. There are workshops on workplace etiquette and basic work skills.
deadline_text: The program page says the application is usually available February to March. In 2026 the deadline passed in March (WVXU reported about two weeks left on March 10, 2026). 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer long term in parks. Jobs include habitat restoration, education programs and special events. You can work on golf course upkeep. You can grow native plants or garden. You can also care for animals. Role training and uniforms are provided.
deadline_text: Long term volunteer information sessions have ended for 2026. Great Parks says it will host them again in March 2027.

what_you_do: You get a paid job and job training all year. Training covers resumes, interviews, work habits, customer service and solving problems.
deadline_text: The county page has a Youth Apply Here link and no closing date. Summer slots can fill early, so apply in winter.

what_you_do: You can volunteer at the Main Library or a branch. You can help with kids and teen events. You can also help with holds, clerical work, technology help and tutoring.
deadline_text: The library volunteer system says it is accepting new volunteer applications. No deadline is posted.

what_you_do: Greet visitors, help guests find their way and cover the museums' gallery spaces, working with museum teams. Teens set their own shifts and can stay until they graduate.
deadline_text: Youth volunteers are recruited each year from January through March. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Help collect data on the maple trees in the sugarbush during maple season. Help tidy the grounds in early spring. Teens ages 14 to 17 can also be Leaders in Training. They help camp counselors, including on nature hikes.
deadline_text: The volunteer page says recruiting and onboarding is closed for the 2026 season and to check back in the new year for 2027 dates.

what_you_do: You improve and maintain trails, parks and community spaces. You remove invasive plants. You learn job readiness and natural resource skills. These skills help in the green industry.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the pages read. The City post is undated.

what_you_do: Two week academies put on a whole play or musical. One week showcases build stage skills, with a focus on acting and telling stories.
deadline_text: The page read listed 2026 camps with an early bird discount through Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You work part time over the summer for the Cincinnati Police Department and learn about police work. The page says it gives help to people who may choose police work as a career.
deadline_text: No current dates are posted on the police page. A January 2024 city news item said the 2024 police cadet application had its own deadline, so check in winter.

what_you_do: Follow a TriHealth staff member for a short look at the job. It is usually about 8 to 16 hours. Shadowing is observation only. You cannot talk with patients in a hands-on way or see their medical records.
deadline_text: No dates or deadlines are posted. Check with the program.

what_you_do: Day camps on the Clifton campus from 9 am to 4 pm. Camps are grouped by age and skill level. The 2026 form named Young Engineers and Rising Engineers camps.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed and late applications were not accepted. Sign up for the interest list to hear about 2027 camps.

what_you_do: Attend a free, in person day camp on UC's main campus. Learn cybersecurity, software development, game development and data and cloud technologies. Hear from IT leaders. Build a team project with a college student mentor.
deadline_text: The camp page says registration is open and that the camp is first come, first served and spots fill up fast. It does not print a deadline or the year, so confirm the dates with the Early IT team.

what_you_do: You learn what hospital jobs are like, both with patients and behind the scenes. You hear from staff, go on tours and join online sessions.
deadline_text: The page links an online application and gives no deadline.

what_you_do: You help patients and visitors, work in waiting rooms and clinics, and do other tasks such as the gift shop. At least 4 hours a week.
deadline_text: UC Medical Center summer applications run April 1 to 30. West Chester summer applications run April 1 to 30; fall applications start in August and spring applications start in December.

what_you_do: Take a week long, full day workshop at the UC College of Medicine. It is for rising high school juniors and seniors. They should be interested in medicine or health care. Tracks are Cellular or Molecular, plus one Medical Informatics session.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was March 25, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.

what_you_do: You work a summer job that teaches responsibility and career readiness. The league also runs a yearly youth summit led by teens.
deadline_text: The page has an Apply Now button and no dates. Dates for summer 2027 are not posted.

what_you_do: You volunteer at the Zoo for the summer. This includes one week of ZooTeen camp. It also includes Visitor Engagement shifts. You also join Lunch and Learns and events.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application is open online Dec 1, 2026 to Jan 31, 2027. Information sessions Nov 16, Dec 14 and Jan 11 (6 to 7 p.m.). Group interviews Feb 27, Feb 28, Mar 13 or Mar 14. Decisions by email April 2, 2027.

what_you_do: Cadets join a local squadron for weekly meetings. They learn leadership, aerospace and fitness. They can take orientation flights and go to events and an encampment.
deadline_text: Join any time. Attend about three meetings, then complete the application.

what_you_do: Cadets meet weekly at a local squadron. They learn leadership, aerospace and fitness. The national page says Saturday events are ideally once a month. There is one week-long encampment in summer.
deadline_text: Join any time. Visit a squadron and attend at least three meetings.

what_you_do: You are in a school-year group. The group visits farms, conservation sites, agriculture businesses and colleges. There are at least six field days. You build resume, interview and speaking skills.
deadline_text: No dates posted. Schools sign up as groups.

what_you_do: You get a year-long paid internship at a school garden. It includes weekly garden hours, a workforce class, field trips to farms and guest speakers.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.

what_you_do: Six evening sessions and one overnight retreat. You meet local, state and national leaders. Topics include community service, arts and the armed forces. Others are business and ethics. You also learn about career paths.
deadline_text: 2026-27 class: orientation Aug 17, 2026, retreat Sept 12-13, evenings Oct 14, Oct 26, Nov 16, Dec 7, Jan 25, Feb 22, Mar 22, graduation Apr 19, 2027. Next application dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Weekly training in criminal law, crime scene work, gun safety, patrol and traffic control. You help at community events. You also compete in cadet contests.
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Dates, times and places may change.

what_you_do: Help at one of 15 Cobb libraries. Roles listed include book finder (shelver), classroom helper and community garden helper. You can also be a greeter or watch the video games.
deadline_text: The page does not list an application deadline.

what_you_do: Juniors and seniors leave school for one or more class periods. They work in a career-related job, internship or youth apprenticeship. They earn school credit. They keep a career portfolio. Employers send evaluations.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Ask your school's coordinator for the application window.

what_you_do: This is a career pathway program for young adults in Cobb County. It offers free education tuition. You get paid work experience and job readiness workshops. You get career coaching. You also get help with GED or diploma.
deadline_text: Year-round. No application dates are posted.

what_you_do: Take free college classes at College of San Mateo while in high school. Dual enrollment is through partner high schools. It includes free books and materials. Concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units a semester.
deadline_text: No application deadline stated on the pages read.

what_you_do: Cadets fly, learn to lead, hike, camp and get in shape. This squadron meets on Wednesday evenings at the College Park Airport.
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join any time through a local squadron.

what_you_do: Advise the City Council on issues that affect kids, teens and families. Meets monthly at places around the city.
deadline_text: No application dates posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer at a hospital you are placed in for a full semester. You work at least 3 hours a week.
deadline_text: The Lanham campus was accepting student applications when read. Deadlines are listed only for the Annapolis campus (Summer May 1, Fall Aug 1, Spring Dec 1).

what_you_do: Six weeks on site at NASA Goddard working with a scientist or engineer on a real project such as robotics, mission software or satellite data analysis.
deadline_text: The application period has closed. The page does not give 2026 or 2027 dates.

what_you_do: Learn branding, marketing and business basics for young artists. It ends with a pitch contest.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the teen programs page.

what_you_do: Join a summer ensemble. It tours Shakespeare plays for families. It plays in parks across Prince George's and Montgomery counties. Professional theater artists mentor you.
deadline_text: The county page lists a March 1, 2027 deadline but does not say whether applications are open, and it has no application link. Email to ask before you plan around it.

what_you_do: Serve on the council for an eight month term. You help curate art projects and presentations. You attend council meetings every two weeks. You also do community service and join an annual art field trip.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026 to 27 term ran Aug 1 to Oct 4, 2026 and are closed. Expect a similar August to early October window next year.

what_you_do: Join a six week summer touring production of an original play. It performs for M-NCPPC summer camps. There is a public show at the end. You rehearse weekly starting in April 2027.
deadline_text: Auditions are on Sunday, February 7, 2027 at 3 p.m. at the Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center (8270 Alumni Dr, College Park).

what_you_do: Grow your skills in theatre, dance and music. It builds leadership skills and leads to shows for the community.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the teen programs page.

what_you_do: Take college classes at PGCC while still in high school and earn college credit.
deadline_text: Spring 2027 application deadline Dec 18, 2026. Summer 2027 deadline Apr 16, 2027. Fall 2027 deadline Jul 16, 2027.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the hospital in 4-hour shifts, working toward 100 hours within 12 months.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The process usually takes about one month.

what_you_do: A two-week summer day camp in advanced math. It is for high school students who are strongly driven.
deadline_text: 2027 dates and deadline not posted.

what_you_do: Stay on campus for a week of lab work, demos, lectures and a team design project. You visit each of the eight engineering departments. Only 25 to 30 students are accepted per session.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was April 24, 2026, with notices by May 15. The 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Use math and machine learning on real problems. Topics include how disease spreads, nature and cancer. You also do hands-on experiments.
deadline_text: The 2026 camp page said the camp was full (posted June 4, 2026). 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: One week of hands-on media work. You do photo stories, interviews and podcasts. You also make short films and social media stories. The week ends with a show of your work.
deadline_text: 2026 camp was Aug 3 to 7, 2026. No registration deadline listed. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Spend three weeks on the UMD campus. You get about 38 hours of SAT prep and 11 hours of college prep. You also hear department talks and join admissions and financial aid workshops. You get one on one help with college applications.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was Friday May 8, 2026, with notices by May 22 and rolling spots after that. The 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Take a three week robotics session. You need no robotics experience. It is for commuters. Topics include drones and 3D nanoprinting. Others are autonomous ground vehicles and soft medical robotics. You earn a non-credit SPARC certificate.
deadline_text: The SPARC page shows an Apply Now banner with a December 1, 2026 deadline. The same page also says applications for this summer are closed, so it is not clear whether applications are open. Confirm with the program first.

what_you_do: One week of learning why volcanoes erupt and which ones are the most dangerous. You do hands-on volcano research.
deadline_text: 2026: applications open until slots filled, acceptances due May 15, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Live on campus for a week and try engineering. You see department talks and demos, do hands-on activities and tour labs. You also join workshops and a weeklong team design project. UMD engineering students mentor you. It is not for credit.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 is full and closed. The page says applications for Summer 2027 will open in January 2027.

what_you_do: One week on the UMD campus learning about forestry jobs by doing. You work with people who do these jobs and experts.
deadline_text: Camp is July 11 to 17, 2027, limited to 30 students. No deadline given; apply as soon as possible.

what_you_do: Teens volunteer at the library. The page does not list tasks.
deadline_text: The page says the teen volunteer program is currently full and that applications for summer volunteering will open April 1. No year is shown.

what_you_do: You learn how giving money for health works. You help pick which youth health programs get grants. Topics include mental health, bullying, basic needs and drug use prevention.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted on the Become a Member page.

what_you_do: Take real college classes at Columbus State while you are in grades 7 to 12. You earn college credit and meet high school graduation rules at the same time.
deadline_text: Public school students turn in a Letter of Intent to their high school by April 1. Homeschool and non-public students apply for state CCP funding by April 1.

what_you_do: Partner groups run summer work programs. Ages 14 to 15 do a 6-week program. Ages 16 to 18 get traditional work experiences. Ages 18 to 21 do paid pre-apprenticeship training.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications were listed as full at every partner. Dates for summer 2027 are not posted.

what_you_do: You explore careers and practice resumes and interviews. You build leadership and money skills. The summer Ready 2 Earn part has coaching, projects and an AI certificate.
deadline_text: Interest form is open now. Monthly sessions run from Nov 18, 2026 to May 6, 2027. Summer 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Help care for shelter animals or help with non-animal tasks after training. Volunteers commit to at least 4 hours a month.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Sign up any time on the volunteer page.

what_you_do: You help library customers sign up for the Summer Reading Challenge. You log reading points. You hand out prizes. You help with programs at a branch.
deadline_text: 2026: application opened April 13 at 3 p.m. and the program ran June 1 to July 31. 2027 dates are not posted. The library's regular volunteer application for Fall 2026 opened August 10.

what_you_do: Volunteer in central Ohio parks, for example as a naturalist, trail volunteer or on wildlife projects. Junior Volunteers at Inniswood Metro Gardens help with flowerbeds and children's programs.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Volunteer Information sessions are held twice a year; the Inniswood training is held in March.

what_you_do: Sort and pack food, help serve in the Mid-Ohio Kitchen, work at the markets or garden, or make kids' meals. Groups and friends can sign up together.
deadline_text: No deadline. Sign up for open shifts any time.

what_you_do: You volunteer one shift a week at a Mount Carmel hospital. You help patients and visitors. Jobs depend on the hospital and when you can come.
deadline_text: The Teen Program runs year-round. No deadline is listed.

what_you_do: You go behind the scenes at the museum and explore modern art. You work with staff to make programs for young people. You also build work skills and learn to speak to the public.
deadline_text: The application for the 2026-27 session has closed. The page says to stay tuned for future opportunities and gives no new dates.

what_you_do: A free, teens-only art workshop at the museum with snacks. A quarterly version called Teen Studio: Unwind is also offered.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Specific dates for Unwind are not listed on the page read.

what_you_do: Help families, patients and staff under supervision at the hospital. You keep one weekly 2 to 3 hour shift from June to mid-August and can move into new assignments if you do well.
deadline_text: The 2026 application opened February 2, 2026 and has reached capacity. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A 2 week camp where you live on campus. You work in small teams and use supercomputers to solve science and engineering problems. Talks cover Unix, Python, cyber safety and supercomputers. You tour Ohio State labs.
deadline_text: Applications open January 15 and close April 1, 2027. Accepted students are told in April.

what_you_do: You take a one-week course on campus, taught by Ohio State faculty, staff and graduate students. Classes meet 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday to Friday and are not for grades or credit.
deadline_text: Check back in early January 2027 for the summer 2027 course list and registration form.

what_you_do: A three-day hands-on camp with practice drills. You visit an anatomy lab and practice what to do in a code blue. You listen to heart and lung sounds and practice intubation. You also try a surgery skills lab and see brain activity demos.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran June 1 to 3, 2026. The page lists an April 24 deadline (no year given, matching the 2026 dates), decisions April 27 to May 8, and orientation May 28. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A one-week day program. Mornings are lectures by Ohio State professors on the mind and brain. Afternoons are group talks and hands-on activities. You also get a taste of college life.
deadline_text: 2026 program ran July 13 to 17, 2026. All 2026 materials were due May 31, 2026, with decisions by June 14. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the next application.

what_you_do: A three-week day camp that gives you a taste of med school. You hear lectures and learn the basics of research. You do a service project and clinical workshops. You also shadow doctors at Wexner Medical Center and Nationwide Children's Hospital.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran June 8 to 26, 2026. 2026 applications were due March 17, 2026 (late ones not accepted). 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You get college advice, coaching, mentors and campus visits from 8th grade through high school. Students who finish in good standing get an Ohio State money package for college.
deadline_text: The page says applications are accepted from prospective 8th graders each year. The 2026-27 deadline is not stated on the part of the page read.

what_you_do: Help keep the library neat, put books on shelves and set up events. You can help at the Homework Help Center and reward readers during Summer Reading. There is more to do too.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply on the volunteer page. Not all roles are open at all times.

what_you_do: You do paid work with City departments and local businesses. Jobs can include helping at summer camps, caring for parks or supporting golf courses. You get mentoring, skill building and career planning.
deadline_text: 2026 participant applications ran Feb 2 to Feb 17, 2026 and are closed. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You learn leadership, teamwork, problem solving and service. You meet monthly from fall to spring. A family orientation is required. There is an end-of-year ceremony.
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Wednesday, July 1, 2026. 2027-28 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Lifeguard jobs are open now. The jobs are seasonal.
deadline_text: The page says the City is hiring seasonal lifeguards for the summer. No application dates are posted.

what_you_do: A six week summer program in math where you live on campus.
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application window has closed. Summer 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Computing Career Corps is a hands-on way to try key tech skills. IT On Ramp+ is a four week, full day program. It builds algebra and geometry skills and confidence.
deadline_text: The page lists IT On Ramp+ sessions June 1 to 26 at Whitehall-Yearling High School and July 6 to 31 at Franklin Heights High School. The page gives no year. Dates for 2027 are not posted.

what_you_do: Help camp counselors with activities for campers in grades 2 to 9. You go on field trips and get daily snacks ready. You do other tasks too. You work at least one week of an eight-week summer camp.
deadline_text: The page does not post an application deadline or interview dates. Contact Meg Brown by email.

what_you_do: A two-week day camp where teens write stories, poems and dialogue with working writers and teachers, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the Thurber Center and Thurber House downtown.
deadline_text: 2026 registration closed July 6, 2026. The page says to check back in the new year for 2027 information.

what_you_do: Teens meet every other Tuesday evening to do writing exercises and share and discuss their own writing. You can join in person or by Zoom.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 sessions: Sep 1, Sep 15, Sep 29, Oct 13, Oct 27 and Nov 10, 2026. No registration deadline is posted.

what_you_do: Teens help with craft kits, library programs and cleaning toys during the school year, and help at the Summer Reading prize table in summer. Teen Service Club sessions earn one hour of service credit.
deadline_text: School-year 2026-2027 teen volunteering is listed as open. The page does not list summer 2027 dates. Teen Service Club dates run from October 19, 2026 into 2027, with registration opening 2 weeks before each date.

what_you_do: You take part in a paid summer youth internship program. It builds empowerment, innovation, high performance and civic engagement skills. Employer partners help run it.
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the program page.

what_you_do: Teens earn service hours by helping library staff. There are two roles. Summer Volunteers give out prizes and help kids sign up to read. Lead Volunteers help at events and get materials ready.
deadline_text: Summer Volunteers (ages 12 to 18, May to July) is marked not yet accepting applications. Lead Volunteers is marked currently full. The page gives no year.

what_you_do: In the school year, sort and shelve materials and help with program supplies and office work. In summer, help patrons join the Summer Reading Club and do special projects.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. The page was last revised August 18, 2026.

what_you_do: You build leadership skills by volunteering. You plan events like blood drives and weekend retreats. You can also join counselor in training programs.
deadline_text: New members are always welcome. No deadline is posted.

what_you_do: An 8-day trip to the Forfar Field Station in the Bahamas with Zoo staff. You study the sea and how to protect it. You snorkel, explore tide pools, and learn about climate change, plastics and jobs in conservation.
deadline_text: Apply by November 22, 2026. Info sessions: in person Nov. 11, 2026 and virtual Nov. 12, 2026 (6:30 to 7:30 p.m.). The Zoo tells students if they were selected by December 4, 2026.

what_you_do: A school team of 4 to 7 high school students plus one advisor spends a kickoff day at the Zoo. The team then builds a Conservation Action Plan for its school or town. It shares the plan at a spring celebration. Teams can apply for grant money.
deadline_text: The application deadline was October 1, 2026. The page does not post a 2027-28 round.

what_you_do: Help guests and learn about conservation careers, with an emphasis on zoo and aquarium customer service. Direct animal contact is minimal.
deadline_text: The 2026 season application has ended. The page says 2027 ZooAide applications will be posted in early 2027.

what_you_do: Teens in grades 9 to 12 go behind the scenes with the education team. They research tech history. They meet Silicon Valley professionals. They lead tours and activities.
deadline_text: Applications are currently closed. Join the interest list to hear about the next round.

what_you_do: Build an app in any language and submit it to your House district. Winners are shown at the US Capitol.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline for registering and submitting is October 26, 2026.

what_you_do: You can take free college classes. There is no cost for tuition, books or enrollment fees. You must attend West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies or Middle College High School. Classes are on campus.
deadline_text: Rolling by term.

what_you_do: Teen roles include Summer Read volunteer, Computer Docent and Homework Help.
deadline_text: Summer Read recruiting starts in April. Some libraries take volunteers on a limited basis.

what_you_do: Give one-on-one tech help as a Teen Tech Tutor, help with local history work like photocopying and data entry, or volunteer in the summer. Younger teens can do service craft programs or join a T(w)een Advisory Board. Volunteer work counts as service hours.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications for Teen Tech Tutors at Aspen Drive Library and Cook Park Library are accepted and reviewed until October 15, 2026. The Summer 2026 youth volunteer application period has closed. The Seed Library role is closed for now.

what_you_do: You greet guests. You also help COSI educators as an operational volunteer. First you apply and do an interview. Then you finish three weekend training sessions.
deadline_text: 2026 window: applications Aug 1 to Aug 15, interviews Sept 15, 16 or 17, decisions Sept 30, trainings Oct 24/25, Nov 21/22 and Dec 12/13. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You spend four weeks living on campus. It is a summer program with college-level math and science courses. You also do hands-on projects.
deadline_text: Application opens Jan 6, 2027 at 8:00 AM and closes Feb 5, 2027 (dates page says 5:00 PM). Financial aid forms postmarked by Feb 6, 2027. Decisions Mar 25, 2027.

what_you_do: Take OCC college classes while in high school, on campus or online (concurrent), or in classes held at a partner high school (CCAP). Classes earn college units and can count toward high school credit.
deadline_text: No fixed date. Apply for the term you want. Forms take at least 7 to 10 business days to process.

what_you_do: You can work part time. You can be a Community Services Leader who runs recreation programs. You can also be a lifeguard or swim instructor. Hours vary. Leaders average 20 hours a week.
deadline_text: Jobs are posted on the city's job page. No dates are stated.

what_you_do: Teen Action Academy is for grades 9 to 12. It plans service projects and teen events. Teen Leadership Committee is for grades 7 to 8. It builds leadership and teamwork.
deadline_text: Not posted on the volunteer page.

what_you_do: You get classroom and hands-on fire training. You practice leadership. You earn community service hours.
deadline_text: Applications for the next school year open in Spring 2027 (no exact date or closing date posted).

what_you_do: Interns help patrons at a library branch. They promote summer programs. They organize spaces and make book lists. Then they co-lead a library program. In 2026, interns were also trained to lead Artist's Studio in the Library with the Art Institute.
deadline_text: The 2026 posting says applications are closed. 2027 dates not posted; the Chicago Youth Works summer application ran March 10 to May 29 in 2026.

what_you_do: These are paid teen assistantships at the library. You pick and promote the year's best teen books. Or you plan a free gaming convention. Or you make social media content in YOUmedia. Teens meet weekly or monthly and finish projects.
deadline_text: Applications open Monday Oct 19, 2026 and close Sunday Nov 8, 2026.

what_you_do: Greet visitors and patients in the main lobby of CPMC Van Ness Campus. Give directions, information and help at the front desk.
deadline_text: The listing shows Actively Recruiting. No application deadline is stated.

what_you_do: You can take career classes in 11 areas. Areas include farm science, construction and business. They also include cooking, teaching and health. Others are IT, law and safety, manufacturing, media, personal care and transportation. You get hands-on learning.
deadline_text: GoCPS high school application dates are not stated on the CTE page; check GoCPS.

what_you_do: This two-year training program is for CPS juniors and seniors. You rotate through carpentry, electricity, HVAC and welding. You earn OSHA 10, CPR and NCCER credentials. In senior year, you do internships. You also prepare for the pre-apprenticeship exam.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application closed April 17, 2026 (decisions by May 22). 2027-28 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Seniors spend the afternoon of a school day at a paid job or internship. It lasts all year. The job matches a career path. You get a personal training plan. A co-op teacher visits the worksite.
deadline_text: Students must apply during junior year. Application dates not stated on the page.

what_you_do: Juniors and seniors take college courses for free. Take them at their own high school (dual credit). Or take them on a City Colleges campus (dual enrollment). Career courses include aviation, construction, culinary, IT and nursing.
deadline_text: Register once per academic year. Deadlines not stated; talk to your counselor early.

what_you_do: This two-year after-school program is for juniors and seniors. You apply as a sophomore. Classes meet twice a week at the Police or Fire Academy. Qualified students can earn OSHA, CPR and EMT-B certifications. It leads to a path into City Colleges.
deadline_text: The application for the class of 2028 is closed. Sophomores apply online each year beginning in February; recruitment events run in February and March. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: This is a month long, pre-professional summer arts program. Students train in one department. Choices are animation, dance, film and music. Others are theater, visual art, writing, or architecture and environment.
deadline_text: 2027 application opens in November (timeline lists Nov 1, 2026). Application and scholarship priority deadline is Feb 28, 2027, 6 pm, with no extensions. Session: registration July 3, classes July 5, graduation July 31, 2027.

what_you_do: Take free college courses and college and career awareness classes from a CUNY campus while in high school. You can take them at your school, on a campus, online, or on Saturdays. Earn up to 15 college credits.
deadline_text: Each campus sets its own deadline. CUNY says spring applications are typically available October to early February, summer March to June, and fall late March to mid-September.

what_you_do: Teen commissioners advise the Cupertino City Council on issues that affect local youth. They attend monthly meetings from September to May.
deadline_text: The city page says recruitment is currently closed. No reopening date is stated.

what_you_do: You can take Red Cross lifeguard training. You can also take a junior lifeguard class. Or try Junior Swim Instructor, where you shadow instructors. This can lead to volunteer chances and city aquatics jobs.
deadline_text: Courses are offered throughout the year. Check WebTrac for sessions.

what_you_do: You referee or keep score at youth basketball games on Saturdays, or coach a team of 3rd to 6th graders. Hours are 5 to 10 a week for officials and 3 to 8 for coaches.
deadline_text: The posting is open continuously. Mandatory training is the week of January 4, 2027 and a coaching clinic on January 9, 2027.

what_you_do: You can take school classes in career pathways. The pathways are in seven industry sectors. Courses come in a sequence. The district also offers student internships through its career program.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Enroll through your counselor during normal course selection.

what_you_do: You plan events and service projects. You learn leadership skills. You speak up on issues that matter to Davis teens.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application period was extended to Oct 2, 2026 and is now closed. The next call is not posted.

what_you_do: Six-week summer volunteer session at the hospital. Greet patients and visitors, help with wayfinding, round with the hospitality cart, and finish a group project.
deadline_text: The application is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027. 2027 session dates are to be determined.

what_you_do: Take De Anza College classes, online or on campus, while in high school. Many courses count toward CSU or UC credit.
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply for admission before the quarter you want; see the De Anza academic calendar.

what_you_do: You can join a school club that prepares you for marketing, finance, hospitality and management careers. It has competitions and conferences.
deadline_text: Join anytime through your advisor.

what_you_do: Train like a firefighter: hose lines, ladders, breathing gear and tools, plus CPR and first aid, fitness and teamwork. After cadet training you may ride along on fire trucks.
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Meeting times are not listed.

what_you_do: You plan and run a teen library project or program. You share ideas at monthly meetings. You help promote reading and library services.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-2027 school year are closed. The page does not say when the next application opens.

what_you_do: Help at recreation centers and sports fields with set-up, check-in, equipment and keeping kids engaged. Shifts are weekday afternoons and Saturdays.
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteer any time.

what_you_do: Take a school class that places you in a paid or unpaid job or internship related to your career goal while you finish high school. Juniors and seniors start this work experience.
deadline_text: No dates are posted. Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator.

what_you_do: These are paid summer internships with county partners. Fields include healthcare, education, technology, retail and government. In 2025, 350 interns worked Monday to Thursday. They worked up to 24 hours a week.
deadline_text: In 2025 registration ran Apr 10 to Apr 20 (11:59 p.m.). No 2026 or 2027 cycle was found on the county site.

what_you_do: Live on campus and train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Trades include carpentry, electrical, culinary arts and facilities maintenance. There are more.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

what_you_do: Teen volunteers run hands-on science exhibits, help at birthday parties and support special events at the science center. Most shifts are on weekends, school holidays and in summer.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply online any time.

what_you_do: You engage guests at exhibits. You lead hands-on activities. You answer visitor questions. You help at events like Bubblefest. You also help with admin tasks and special projects.
deadline_text: Teen application is closed right now. The page says to check back on December 1, 2026 for winter/spring 2027 details.

what_you_do: You take a school course with weekly coaching on resumes, cover letters and interviews. You get an unpaid internship or prep for paid work. Sites include Davis Public Library, Davis Vanguard, Mercy General and Pemberton Engineering.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. 2026-27 sites are listed now.

what_you_do: Help the camp counselor and campers with games, crafts and hikes at Lyman Woods. You can also help at after-school and special programs. Other roles are restoration and garden work. There is also an office role at the interpretive center.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Call 630-963-9388 for Lyman Woods volunteer details.

what_you_do: Teens help City of Dublin camp staff. They help during summer camps and swim lessons. They get training in job skills. They learn to lead activities, water safety and supervising campers.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Dublin teens give the City input. The input is on its programs and activities for young people. The committee meets monthly. It usually meets on the second Wednesday at the Dublin Senior Center.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 seats are filled (term June 2026 to May 2027). The city page we read does not post a recruitment date for the 2027-28 term.

what_you_do: This is six weeks of paid summer research in a Duke cell biology lab. You work with a graduate student or postdoc. You do your own project. There are career seminars and journal clubs.
deadline_text: The page says Summer 2026 applications are closed and Summer 2027 applications will be accepted in January 2027. 2026 deadline: the flyer says March 20, 2026 and the FAQ says March 27, 2026 at 5 pm.

what_you_do: This is a two-day hospital event for high school students. It has facility tours. It has hands-on CPR training and career activities. Students earn 14 volunteer hours and a certificate.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened 8 pm Friday April 10 and closed 8 pm Monday April 13, 2026; acceptance emails by May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: A hybrid summer internship at Duke Health. In 2026 students spent three weeks touring clinical spaces, learning skills and hearing from Duke employees about their careers.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: Durham YouthWorks application opened January 23 and closed February 21, 2026; orientation in March. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Duke runs residential summer academic programs on its campus. They are for high school students. Students must be at least 14 to attend.
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Full payment is due 30 days before each session; immunization proof due June 1, 2027; full refund for cancellations before April 1, 2027.

what_you_do: Help adult staff run nature camp: daily camp tasks and time with young campers, and help at events if you want. Full-day or half-day shifts.
deadline_text: The page says applications opened in Spring 2026. No deadline is listed. If applications are closed, your info is kept until the next open period.

what_you_do: Help kids and families at the children's museum. Teen volunteers (14 and up) take flexible shifts. Junior volunteers (junior high) help one weekend day a week for three months.
deadline_text: Junior volunteers are recruited in September and January. Teen and adult openings are posted on the museum site.

what_you_do: Volunteer in the forest preserves. Jobs include one-time restoration workdays and special events. You can also help at nature centers, farms and historic sites. Teens 13 to 17 have a few long-term roles.
deadline_text: No single deadline. Some roles have deadlines and limited space. New volunteer orientation is held monthly at district headquarters (second Wednesday evening).

what_you_do: Volunteers help staff run pre-made maker programs and workshops. They run equipment trainings. They help at service desks.
deadline_text: No deadline. Capacity is limited, so you may be put on a waitlist.

what_you_do: Teens help at a library branch with shelving, pulling books, tutoring and prepping crafts. Tasks depend on the branch and the time.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Each branch decides whether it can host volunteers; availability is not guaranteed.

what_you_do: Free American Red Cross lifeguard training (worth $209). It covers CPR/AED and first aid. Graduates can apply for lifeguard jobs at Durham's indoor and outdoor pools.
deadline_text: Spring 2026 course: pre-course swim test Sunday, March 15, registration deadline March 15 at 10 am. New dates are posted each season.

what_you_do: Sign up for hands-on volunteer work. Choose park and trail projects, like trail help, landscaping and adopt-a-park. Or help DPR staff at special events like Earth Day and festivals.
deadline_text: No deadline. Browse and sign up for open shifts.

what_you_do: Start with a pre-apprenticeship to try a field. Then move into an apprenticeship that mixes classes with on-the-job training. Apprentices earn wages that rise as their skills grow.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Take college classes for free while in high school and earn both high school and college credit. Pick a college transfer path or a career and technical path (a certificate or diploma).
deadline_text: Spring 2027: application opened Sept 11 and closes Nov 9 (2026). Paperwork due Nov 23. Last day to register Dec 1. Spring semester starts Jan 11, 2027.

what_you_do: You can volunteer at a youth group. You can also do a student internship there. The group offers life coaching, school partnerships and community organizing.
deadline_text: Not posted

what_you_do: You get a paid 6 week summer internship at the water utility. It is about 16 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 East Bay program: no direct applications, referrals from partner groups only. 2027 not posted.

what_you_do: You can get seasonal paid student jobs such as recreation leader, lifeguard, gate attendant, student laborer and interpretive student aide. The jobs include pathways from high school to college.
deadline_text: No jobs were posted on governmentjobs.com on Oct 7, 2026. Watch ebparks.org/jobs/youth and governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks.

what_you_do: You can take college courses at Elgin Community College. You can also take them at your high school. You earn high school and college credit at the same time. Options include general education and career tech courses.
deadline_text: No deadline on the ECC page. Talk with your high school counselor about dates.

what_you_do: Get help planning for college and careers. You choose classes, explore careers, set goals and prep for tests. You get help with college and aid forms. There are college tours and workshops for parents.
deadline_text: No deadline. Spots are first come, first served, so apply as early as possible.

what_you_do: This is free college prep for high school students. It includes advising, educational workshops and tutoring. It also includes field trips and college courses. You get fee waivers for college applications and SAT/ACT.
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.

what_you_do: You join an after-school environmental justice program for Berkeley teens and young adults (8 weeks in summer or 12 weeks in spring). Topics include zero waste, climate resilience and food systems. It is paid.
deadline_text: No dates on the Ecology Center page. Berkeley YouthWorks listed a Winter 2027 interest form due Oct 30, 2026 and said Summer 2027 information comes in Feb 2027, but that page does not mention this academy.

what_you_do: You take career classes during high school at the Eden Area ROP career center in Hayward or at some home high schools. Class choices include welding, auto, construction, culinary arts, dental assisting, cybersecurity, first responder and education careers.
deadline_text: Enroll through your home school counselor; the page gives no class start dates.

what_you_do: Live on campus and train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes IT certifications (A+, AWS Cloud Practitioner), plumbing, bricklayer and more.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

what_you_do: Take real college courses during the school day, on campus or online. You earn college credit while still in high school.
deadline_text: No deadline listed on the page.

what_you_do: Teens meet each month on the teen board. They help shape library services. They also find volunteer opportunities. The library calls TAB the starting point for teen volunteering.
deadline_text: Monthly. The listing shows the next session as Wednesday, October 14, 7:00 to 8:30 p.m., Main Library Children's Room.

what_you_do: Spend one 4 to 5 hour shift a week at the hospital through the summer. Juniors do things like escorting patients and delivering items. Older adult volunteers work with you and mentor you.
deadline_text: Last cycle's pattern: names taken in April, interviews in May, orientation in June, program ends end of July. 35 students took part in 2025.

what_you_do: Take college classes for credit while still in high school.
deadline_text: Register each term. Fall 2026 8-week classes starting in October were still open when read. Winter Session (Jan 4 to Feb 4, 2027) and Spring Semester (Feb 16 to Jun 12, 2027) registration opens in November 2026.

what_you_do: You can join a year-long hospital volunteer program for teens in Mountain View and Los Gatos.
deadline_text: No application deadline posted. The page says to check back in mid-January 2027 for signup for the next Junior Application Seminar.

what_you_do: Learn firefighter and paramedic skills in class and hands-on. Topics include CPR, first aid, fitness, breathing gear, search and rescue and fire fighting. Help at community events. Uniform and gear are provided.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Come to a meeting (1st or 3rd Wednesday at 6:00 p.m.) to get an application.

what_you_do: Help at the nature center. Tasks include greeting visitors, office work, planting native plants and removing invasive plants. You can also care for trails, lead bird walks, watch wildlife and help with programs. Staff train you.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Train each week in court rules, CPR and crime prevention. You also learn to collect evidence and patrol. Help the police at special events. Do fingerprinting at community events and open houses.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted twice a year. Dates are not posted. Email hector.gutierrez@elginil.gov or edwin.alva@elginil.gov for the next opening.

what_you_do: Join a monthly activity with Elgin police officers. Each month brings a different fun activity. Teens and officers get to know each other.
deadline_text: No deadline. Watch the calendar and social media for dates.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the library or earn service hours. The Junior Teen Advisory Group does service projects and creates teen programs. It also gives book talks, makes promo videos and goes on field trips.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Reading Program volunteer details are announced in January.

what_you_do: Advise the City Council on youth needs. Commissioners meet monthly, meet with their Councilmember, plan youth events and report to the Council.
deadline_text: No open recruitment as of Oct 7, 2026. Seats are filled when openings come up, and the City posts a notice with a Youth Commission application.

what_you_do: You volunteer one weekday shift a week in the same hospital department over the summer. You attend at least four speaker sessions or tours. It is volunteering, not shadowing.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened Feb 17 and closed Feb 27, 2026 (or earlier if full). 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You take a college course taught by Emory faculty. It runs two to four weeks in summer. You can choose residential or commuter. A 3-week Pre-Med Institute is offered. So are 6-week credit courses.
deadline_text: Applications for 2027 open in December 2026. Deadlines: noncredit sessions May 3, 2027; Pre-Med Institute Feb 1, 2027; credit Summer College April 20 and June 7, 2027.

what_you_do: Work one-on-one with a cancer researcher in an active lab for six weeks. You also go to talks, field trips and survivor roundtables. At the end you present your project at a symposium.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle is closed. The page says to check back in fall 2026 for the 2027 cycle. Notices went out by the first week of April.

what_you_do: Help patients and visitors in the hospital as a student volunteer. You might be a greeter or work in the gift shop. Roles differ by location.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The student form says more students apply than there are spots.

what_you_do: Help patients and visitors in the hospital as a teen volunteer, for example as a greeter or in the gift shop. Roles differ by location.
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the pages read.

what_you_do: Help patients and visitors in the hospital. You might be a greeter or work in the gift shop. Other departments need help too. Roles differ by location.
deadline_text: Rolling. Applications are held for one year. The summer 2026 program was full, so summer applications were closed when read.

what_you_do: Help patients and visitors in the hospital. You might be a greeter or work in the gift shop. Other departments need help too. Roles differ by location.
