what_you_do: You attend Wednesday night meetings and training. You go on ride-alongs. You help with traffic and crowd control at events. You join Explorer competitions.
deadline_text: Applications are taken twice a year, in January and July (page gives no exact dates). The next window is expected in January 2027.

what_you_do: You get practical police training, volunteer at community events, and compete in statewide Explorer competitions with police scenarios. Officers and dispatchers lead the program.
deadline_text: No deadline posted.

what_you_do: You go to weekly meetings with law enforcement. You do physical training and go on ride-alongs. You do community service details. You also attend conferences.
deadline_text: No intake dates posted. Contact the coordinator.

what_you_do: This is a free 4-week residential summer program at Pomona College. After that, there is year-round involvement for three years. It helps local students prepare for selective colleges.
deadline_text: Applications open Nov 9, 2026 and are due Feb 22, 2027 (recommendations due Mar 1, 2027). Decisions Apr 16, 2027.

what_you_do: You volunteer one shift a week in the hospital. It helps you explore medical careers.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The same page says the hospital is currently only accepting adult volunteer applications, so check before applying.

what_you_do: At a children's museum, you can volunteer in administration, field trips or special events. You can also lead a short activity for kids. You can be a TeensTeach or TeensTable teen presenter.
deadline_text: No deadline. Teen program submissions are rolling and spots are limited.

what_you_do: Student volunteers help at library branches. The page says there is a wide range of activities but does not list them.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Pitch your own workshop or activity for other teens and families. If chosen, library staff help you shape it, promote it and present it at a library branch. Builds planning and public speaking skills.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 submissions are open Sept 21 to Oct 31, 2026. The spring window is Feb 1 to Feb 28, 2027. Online info session Oct 13, 2026, 5-6 pm.

what_you_do: You can volunteer on library projects in Queens. Roles can be ongoing or one-day events. Hours earn community service credit. You can ask for a Service Verification Letter.
deadline_text: Minors can apply year-round. Approval and placement can take up to 30 days, longer in summer and fall.

what_you_do: You take a Red Cross course on caring for infants and children, safety and emergencies. The online option also covers starting a babysitting business.
deadline_text: Ongoing.

what_you_do: You can take Red Cross courses for lifeguarding or swim instruction. Lifeguard students must be 15 by the last day of class and pass a swimming skills test.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Class dates depend on the provider.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the library in fall, winter/spring or summer sessions, or at one-day community events. You can earn community service hours.
deadline_text: No specific dates posted. Email to ask what is open now.

what_you_do: Volunteer in the hospital in a placement, at least one 2-hour shift a week. Some assignments have after-school, early evening or weekend shifts.
deadline_text: The page says junior recruitment opens from time to time during the year. No dates posted.

what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes human services and collision repair. It includes carpentry and electrical. There are more.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

what_you_do: Teens ages 13 to 15 get training. Then they help camp staff with kids at Redwood City summer camps. Activities include group games, sports, arts and crafts and field trips.
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened April 20 and were due May 8, 2026; interviews May 18 to 21; training June 13. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: It is the world's largest pre-college science fair. You first win a spot at a local fair affiliated with the Society for Science, then compete at ISEF in 22 categories.
deadline_text: ISEF is in Los Angeles in May 2027 (exact dates not posted on the pages read). Affiliated fairs end by mid-April, and each fair sets its own deadline, so find yours now.

what_you_do: High school seniors submit an independent research project. The top 300 get recognition. The top 40 compete in Washington for awards.
deadline_text: Applications close Nov 5, 2026 at 8 p.m. ET (opened June 1, 2026). Top 300 announced Jan 7, 2027; Top 40 announced Jan 21, 2027; finals week Mar 11 to 17, 2027.

what_you_do: Spend 5 days on campus. You practice hands-on health care skills like CPR, stitching and head-to-toe exams. You also explore careers with RFU graduate students in medicine, pharmacy, nursing and physical therapy.
deadline_text: The page gives no application dates. The camp runs during the last week of July.

what_you_do: Spend 8 weeks doing original biomedical research. A graduate student mentor and a faculty advisor guide you. Daily sessions and weekly workshops cover health care careers, writing, math and science. You can return each summer through college.
deadline_text: The INSPIRE 2026 application is closed. The page says the INSPIRE 2027 application will open in December 2026.

what_you_do: Take part in an 8 week summer program, four days a week. It explores nursing careers and college prep. It includes nursing assistant training. Then you can take the Certified Nursing Assistant exam.
deadline_text: The page still shows the last cycle it read: applications opened December 10, 2024 and closed January 23, 2025. Newer dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Learn core lab techniques and the scientific method in 9 Saturday sessions on campus. Lunch and transportation are provided. Up to 25 students join each summer.
deadline_text: The Science Saturdays 2026 application is closed. For 2027 the application will open in December 2026.

what_you_do: Get matched with a current Rosalind Franklin University student. They mentor you about health care or science careers. After an orientation, you meet once a month by Zoom or phone from October to May.
deadline_text: Registration closes November 30, 2026.

what_you_do: Team up with other teens and library staff to plan programs and help choose teen books.
deadline_text: Registration was full on the page read. Next intake date not stated.

what_you_do: A one-week summer day camp. You learn about police duties, the legal system, criminal justice, fitness and teamwork.
deadline_text: 6th academy is planned for August 2027. Applications posted late 2026 to early 2027. Due April 6, 2027.

what_you_do: Take four college level health science courses full time at KPU Surrey from February to June of Grade 12. You earn high school and university credit.
deadline_text: Application form posted fall 2026. Due March 9, 2027 for the 2027-28 school year.

what_you_do: Take four business courses that transfer to a university. They are marketing, talking at work, how groups work, and accounting. You go full time at KPU Surrey in semester 2.
deadline_text: Applications for 2027-28 are available. Due date not found on the page read. The page says applications are due the year before.

what_you_do: Start Level 1 trades training at a college while still in high school. You earn high school and college credit. You are signed up as an apprentice with SkilledTradesBC.
deadline_text: Applications for 2027-28 are open. Preferred deadline Feb 2, 2027. Second deadline Mar 2, 2027.

what_you_do: Get paid work in a SkilledTradesBC trade and earn high school credit for it. Your work hours count toward an apprenticeship.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Learn how City departments work and how decisions get made. Teams build a project and present it to a mock City Council.
deadline_text: 2026 session was July 7 to 9, 2026. Next dates not posted.

what_you_do: A free media lab with drop in times and skill sessions. You can learn animation, digital drawing and film editing. Later you can use your skills on real jobs like event photos and DJing.
deadline_text: No deadline. Drop-ins: Tue 4-6pm, Thu 4-6pm, Sat 12-4pm.

what_you_do: You get a paid internship of up to 100 hours. It is with local businesses, government or nonprofits. You also get workshops and career coaching.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The 2026-2027 application is posted.

what_you_do: This is a paid job making home energy and water efficiency visits. The visits are called Green House Calls. Then you do an externship at groups such as GRID Alternatives or Berkeley Lab.
deadline_text: No application dates posted. Check risingsunopp.org/jobs for postings.

what_you_do: Help around the library with craft prep and light cleaning. Or be a Book Buddy. You are paired with a young reader entering grades 1 to 3.
deadline_text: The Summer 2026 deadline was Friday, May 1 and the page says Summer 2026 applications are now closed. 2027 dates are not posted yet.

what_you_do: At many branches, teens plan library programs and help in the library. They meet during the year.
deadline_text: Not posted. Contact your local branch.

what_you_do: A 20-week city program with 120 hours of training, job shadowing, mentors, site tours and on-the-job work. You earn a certificate of completion and CPR and First-Aid certification.
deadline_text: The announcement said the next group would start in summer 2025 with recruitment in early spring. No newer dates found.

what_you_do: A city youth center with tutoring, SAT and college application help, FAFSA help, computer access, camps and volunteer chances. Teens in Action is the free afterschool program for 13 to 18 year olds.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No dates or deadlines posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer at city recreation programs. You work next to city staff, learn job skills and learn how the city runs. You may get a chance to be hired by the department afterward.
deadline_text: No start dates or deadline posted. The page says the department is looking for participants now.

what_you_do: Volunteer at a City of Riverside library branch. Teens 14 and older can apply. Use the City volunteer portal.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time.

what_you_do: You get 10 hours of training, then up to 50 hours of job experience helping with summer programs, camps and classes.
deadline_text: Interest application and recommendation letter due May 5, 2027. Program starts in June 2027.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the Roseville Public Library. Library staff talk with you after you send the Volunteer Form and decide what you will do.
deadline_text: Rolling.

what_you_do: Help the teen librarian plan teen programs, pick new books and promote events. Members volunteer at library programs at least 3 times a year. They earn community service hours.
deadline_text: The page says no positions are open now. An application form is posted when positions open. No dates are given.

what_you_do: Work one or two shifts a week to help with the library's Summer Reading Challenge. Each shift is 2 to 2.5 hours. It runs in June and July.
deadline_text: 2026 registration is closed. The page also says to check back April 2 (year not stated), so confirm with the teen librarian.

what_you_do: Take a lifeguard class, then work as a lifeguard at city pools. The city also hires pool attendants, swim teachers and cashiers. There is a path from pool attendant to lifeguard.
deadline_text: No application deadline is listed. The 2026 classes ran Mar 16 to May 30, 2026. 2027 class dates are not posted on the page I read.

what_you_do: You join a free summer program for 100 top students. It has one week of STEM classes, five weeks of individual research with a mentor, and one week of reports and presentations.
deadline_text: RSI 2027 applications are open through 11:59 p.m. on December 11, 2026. No late applications.

what_you_do: Help in areas like the gift shop, greeting and escort services, office support and patient care areas. Teens support staff and patients with comfort and friendly help. They do not do medical tasks.
deadline_text: The page said it was accepting applications for the 2026 summer program. Applications are kept on file for 3 months. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer in hospital areas such as information desks and the emergency room. You can also help in the lab, nursing, same day surgery and physical therapy. You get real hospital work experience. Parking is free.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.

what_you_do: You can join the free RYSE youth center for arts, health, organizing and career programs. Members can apply for paid seasonal internships.
deadline_text: Membership: join at an enrollment session. Cohorts and internships have separate windows (see notes).

what_you_do: You clean dog kennels. You do laundry and dishes. You bag pet food for the pantry. You organize donations at the city animal shelter. The shelter can verify school community service hours.
deadline_text: Rolling.

what_you_do: You get career planning and workforce workshops. You also get case management. You can get paid work experience. Examples are internships, job shadowing and part-time work.
deadline_text: No deadline posted.

what_you_do: You get training in teamwork, lesson planning and recreation activities. Completing it helps you apply for the city's Seasonal Rec Aide job.
deadline_text: Winter 2026 registration opened Dec 22, 2025. The page still shows only that session; the next session is not posted.

what_you_do: You do paid weekend crew work in city parks, with training. Tasks include weeding, trimming, and leaf and trash removal.
deadline_text: The page said the Fall 2026 recruitment would begin in July 2026 and last two weeks or until 350 applications. That window is over. The next window is not posted.

what_you_do: You join a paid six-week program. It covers communication, teamwork, leadership and money skills. There are optional bonus workshops.
deadline_text: The program page is out of date. It still shows fall 2025 sessions (registration opened September 8, 2025). Email NNworkforce@cityofsacramento.org to ask about the next session before you apply.

what_you_do: You join an eight-week workforce readiness program. You also plan a community service project.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 registration opened Aug 17, 2026. Summer 2027 sessions: details to come.

what_you_do: Help at a Sacramento Public Library branch with daily branch work, events and programs. You can drop in or take a scheduled spot.
deadline_text: Rolling. The library says processing takes about a month and placement can take 2 to 3 months.

what_you_do: You can take one-week summer academies. Topics include coding, engineering and robotics. There are also health careers and starting a business. Fashion and fire and emergency services are topics too. The list goes on.
deadline_text: The 2027 schedule is posted in January 2027. Online registration opens Monday, March 1, 2027. No closing date stated.

what_you_do: This is a six-week summer program about local government. You take daily classes with teachers. Classes run Mon to Thu, 9 am to 2 pm. In the afternoons, you do internships at city locations.
deadline_text: Application opens Apr 1, 2027 and closes Apr 12, 2027. Interviews start Apr 19, orientation May 22, program starts June 14, 2027. Dates are tentative.

what_you_do: Serve on the youth advisory group that gives the City Council and the Mayor advice on youth policies and programs. About 19 members.
deadline_text: Apply when a seat is open. No dates posted.

what_you_do: Run games, crafts and animal activities at education stations in the zoo and teach guests about animals and conservation.
deadline_text: Applications opened online Oct 10, 2026 for Zoo Teens 2027 (Jan to April). Closing date not stated.

what_you_do: Inspect, sort and repack food and help hand it out at the food bank's distribution center.
deadline_text: Online calendar with open shifts.

what_you_do: This Metro Fire page lists local youth fire programs: City of Sacramento Firefighter Youth Academy, Cosumnes Explorers, and school fire pathways at Del Campo, SAVA, Inderkum and Valley High.
deadline_text: Varies by program. Spring 2027 for the Sacramento academy and Cosumnes Explorers.

what_you_do: Youth groups and students can do community service projects from home. These do not involve working with the animals.
deadline_text: Rolling.

what_you_do: You can get job search help. You can get career workshops, resume and interview coaching and mentoring. You can get training and paid work experience.
deadline_text: Recruitment is year-round.

what_you_do: You can drop in at this youth center. It offers mentoring. It has classes like sewing, English Club and robotics. It also has job training with hands-on work. You can earn community service hours and volunteer.
deadline_text: No application deadline. Classes have their own start dates (for example Robotics Oct 3 and Sewing Oct 16; the page shows no year).

what_you_do: Volunteer at a neighborhood library. You can be a reading mentor. You can be a homework tutor. You can be a tech assistant. Other roles are teen mentor, garden helper and library assistant.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Paid summer jobs and internships. YJ1 places teens in rec centers, pools, libraries, gardening and nonprofits. YJ2 is for ages 16 and up in business, health, trades and other career fields.
deadline_text: Youth apply online February 1-28 for summer. The page does not print the year, so confirm the dates for 2027.

what_you_do: Work in a Salk research lab for eight weeks, 30 to 40 hours a week, as a paid intern.
deadline_text: Applications open Dec 1, 2026 and close Feb 15, 2027.

what_you_do: Volunteer at least 100 hours over the school year in hospital departments, with one 3-hour shift a week.
deadline_text: Page says applications are closed. It lists a deadline of July 30, 2026 and also an application window opening June 1, 2027 (notices by July 29, 2027, interviews Aug 2 to 13, 2027). The dates conflict, so confirm.

what_you_do: You volunteer at your branch library. You build leadership skills. Teen volunteers must attend one monthly Teen Leadership meeting.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Candidates are told the result within 4 to 6 weeks. Meetings are listed from Aug 2026 through May 2027.

what_you_do: Youth volunteers help with traffic control and aviation duties. They also do clerical work, ATV training and crowd control. You go to monthly meetings. You finish the Explorer Academy.
deadline_text: No deadline posted.

what_you_do: Work a paid summer job in a San Bernardino County department while joining workshops, mentoring and career exploration. You earn a certificate of completion.
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened March 16 and closed at the first 800 applications or March 27, whichever came first. 2025 applications opened March 15. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You can get free help with job skills and leadership. You also get help with career exploring, mentoring and work experience. A local youth provider in your part of the county offers it.
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings depend on each provider's capacity, so call the provider that serves your city.

what_you_do: Start as a Tide Pool Interpreter or Greeter. You talk with visitors about ocean animals and their homes. You share the science done at Scripps Institution of Oceanography.
deadline_text: Applications are taken on a rolling basis. Volunteers are trained four times a year. The next onboarding starts with a virtual info session in early 2027.

what_you_do: Volunteer at a national park. Roles include removing invasive plants and greeting visitors. You can help with Junior Ranger programs and protect tide pools. You can also guide science activities.
deadline_text: Group projects are open year-round. No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Work as an intern in a City of San Diego department. Current postings include Stormwater, Engineering and Police roles. You get an orientation at the start. You also get mentoring.
deadline_text: Internships are posted one at a time. On Oct 9, 2026, six internship postings were listed with closing dates from Oct 14 to Oct 30, 2026.

what_you_do: Learn about local government and build leadership skills. You meet in person once a month and online every week. You do volunteer projects, go on City job shadows and join skill workshops.
deadline_text: No deadline is listed on the application page.

what_you_do: You work at city pools. Recreation Aides give customer service to the aquatics community. They train to be lifeguards. Pool Guards need no certification.
deadline_text: Year-round hiring. Pool Guard hiring events are monthly; Recreation Aide interviews are quarterly.

what_you_do: Advise the Mayor and City Council about youth issues. Examples are school, jobs, housing and mental health. You learn about city life, public policy and leadership. You also practice networking.
deadline_text: The page says some of the 20 seats are unfilled and invites youth to apply. No deadline is listed.

what_you_do: You help branch staff organize library materials. You take part in library events. You earn community service hours and work experience.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Ask your branch.

what_you_do: Take college classes for credit while still in high school. Classes can count for both high school and college. You can take up to 11 units (4 classes) on campus or online.
deadline_text: Start at least one month before the semester or session. No set deadline on the page.

what_you_do: Help pack and hand out food. In the Distribution Center, volunteers are 6 and up. At food distributions out in the community, volunteers are 14 and up.
deadline_text: No deadline.

what_you_do: Learn firefighting skills in classes taught by SDFD staff, such as hose lays, ladders, search and rescue, CPR and first aid. Certified cadets can do ride-alongs with fire crews. A one week academy runs each summer.
deadline_text: New cadets are accepted quarterly. No dates are posted.

what_you_do: Sort and bag produce, pack food boxes and bags, and help at community food distributions. No training needed. A short orientation starts each shift.
deadline_text: No deadline. All volunteer visits must be scheduled in advance.

what_you_do: Take an acting intensive with Playhouse artists. Rising 8th and 9th graders do a 9 day program. Rising 10th to 12th graders do a 3 week program with advanced training.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Apr 6, 2026. Summer 2027 applications are expected to open on or around Feb 1, 2027. 2027 dates are not set.

what_you_do: Join a group of high schoolers who learn how a pro theater works. You see shows and meet artists. You plan events that bring young people to the Playhouse.
deadline_text: 2026/27 applications ran Aug 3 to Sept 4, 2026. Next year is not posted yet; expect a similar late summer window.

what_you_do: Help professional educators run summer camps at the museum. The camps are for Pre-K through 8th grade.
deadline_text: Page says recruitment for camp aides begins in May. No 2027 dates posted.

what_you_do: Take real college classes at Palomar on campus or online while you are in high school. Dual enrollment classes can also be taught at some high schools. The classes count toward a college certificate or degree.
deadline_text: No single deadline. Check the Palomar calendar for each term.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the Poway or Escondido hospital. The page lists general roles such as lobby ambassador, escort, desk, book cart and rehab, but does not say which are open to juniors. You complete at least 100 service hours.
deadline_text: Applications are taken all year.

what_you_do: Help with park clean-ups, tree planting, youth sports and recreation programs. You can also help at community events. There are roles at Tecolote Nature Center, aquatics, golf and AgeWell Services.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: A volunteer role with no police powers. Cadets train twice a month and go on ride-alongs. They help with traffic control and security at community events.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Recruiting meetings are held on the second Tuesday of each month at 5 p.m.

what_you_do: Join a branch Teen Team. Help library staff plan and lead programs, support teen outreach at community events, and work on special projects.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time through the City volunteer system.

what_you_do: A free after-school and summer program. You get tutoring, mentoring and college workshops and tours. You also go on service trips, try career experiences and practice public speaking. The page says partners offer access to internships and college courses.
deadline_text: Applications are taken all year. All applicants are added to a waitlist, and staff follow up with next steps.

what_you_do: Work for 8 weeks on a real computing research project with a UC San Diego mentor and grad students. You learn to test ideas with code and finish with a scientific poster.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.

what_you_do: Volunteer at Sharp Grossmont Hospital for at least one year, with one shift a week or two shifts a month.
deadline_text: As of Oct 9, 2026 the page says it is no longer accepting applicants from the high school class of 2028. That means current 9th and 10th graders (classes of 2029 and 2030) may still apply. No deadline is posted.

what_you_do: Greet and guide patients and families, help on nursing units with phones and errands, work in a gift shop, or join Arts for Healing programs. Shifts are 3 to 4 hours a week.
deadline_text: The high school application is closed, and the page does not say when it will reopen. The adult application reopens Oct 19.

what_you_do: Take live online bioengineering courses with a loaner lab kit. Start with an intro course, then a research workshop, then plan and carry out your own project with a university lab.
deadline_text: Winter 2027 application deadline Dec 18, 2026, with a last call through Jan 3, 2027. Space is limited and may fill sooner.

what_you_do: Help patients and staff in hospitals and clinics. Tasks include moving patients, running errands, stocking and lab deliveries. You also greet visitors and visit with patients.
deadline_text: Year-round application. Summer-only applicants must apply between Mar 1 and Apr 15, and say so on the application.

what_you_do: Take live online ocean science courses in three levels. Level 1 teaches marine biology. Level 2 is hands-on research with Scripps graduate students. Level 3 builds science writing and a chance to publish.
deadline_text: Winter 2027 applications are listed as coming soon. The Fall 2026 deadline (Sept 17, 2026) has passed.

what_you_do: You can sign up for free career centers. They offer training and one-on-one coaching. Some people get paid on-the-job work experience.
deadline_text: No deadline. The online application takes about 10 to 15 minutes, then staff contact you about next steps.

what_you_do: Juniors and seniors take 2 to 3 free college classes. Those are 6 to 9 college credits. They also take 4 high school classes. This is on the San Jose City College campus. You earn a high school diploma and transferable college credit.
deadline_text: Not stated on the San Jose City College page. Ask the Middle College office for the application timeline.

what_you_do: Join Teens Reach, the library youth council, to help with kids crafts and Summer Learning sign-ups and to speak up as a library advisor. Or earn service hours by writing book reviews as a Teen Book Reviewer.
deadline_text: Rolling. Each branch has its own Teens Reach sign-up. No single deadline.

what_you_do: You can get paid work experience and job help in San Jose. If you are 14 to 18 and face barriers to work, you can be placed in paid jobs and training. Job services are open to ages 16 to 29.
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the city pages. Apply any time with the online youth application.

what_you_do: Teens advise the San Jose Mayor and City Council on youth issues. The Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is open now; Youth Commission recruitment is closed.
deadline_text: Youth Advisory Council (open now): no deadline posted. Youth Commission (closed): recruitment is closed, no reopening date posted.

what_you_do: You help library staff run programs for younger kids, or help with kit assembly, shelving and displays. You work one shift of 2 to 3 hours a week.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in November 2026. Summer applications open in mid March, per the summer page.

what_you_do: You give the City Council feedback. The feedback is on issues that affect young people. You help run city events like Pumpkin Splash and the Egg Hunt.
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.

what_you_do: You can take free job-skills workshops. You can use a members-only job and internship board. There are twenty $2,000 scholarships a year for San Mateo County youth. The county summer internship is for ages 18 to 21.
deadline_text: Membership: register any time. Summer internship: 2026 applications are closed; the page says next summer opens early 2027 (no date posted). Scholarship deadline not stated.

what_you_do: Teens shelve books, help with kids' crafts and STEM programs, join outreach events or support the makerspace.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Openings vary by branch and there may be a waiting period.

what_you_do: Spend six summer weeks as a fully paid intern in a biomedical research lab.
deadline_text: Next application dates not posted on the page. Use the Request Info form or email the program director.

what_you_do: Work in a city department. Go to quarterly workshops to build job skills. Build mentor ties with department leaders. The city lists a Student Intern level for people enrolled in high school.
deadline_text: The city recruits interns about once a year or as needed. No dates are listed on the page.

what_you_do: Volunteer in City of Santa Ana departments. Fill out the volunteer handbook forms and apply through the city volunteer page. Some roles involve working with children.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Get a paid work placement at a public agency or a local group. The Youth Service Corps version works on climate action and food access. It also works on school and public service projects.
deadline_text: Conflicting city pages. The main program page says applications are now open, while the interest page says the program is currently closed to new applications and offers a form to get a notice when it reopens. Call (714) 565-2600 to confirm before applying.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the zoo, either as a short-term Zoo Greeter or in a long-term role. Younger teens can join as a Zoo Buddies pair with a parent or guardian.
deadline_text: No deadline. Long-term volunteers do an online and an in-person orientation offered every other month.

what_you_do: Join weekly squadron meetings. You get hands-on flight time, STEM projects and leadership milestones. Cadets can serve on search and rescue missions as a Ground Team Member or Mission Radio Operator. They can also help at community events.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron to schedule a visit.

what_you_do: Volunteer with dogs, cats, the clinic or outreach. You go through a virtual meeting, orientation and role training, then start solo shifts.
deadline_text: No deadline. The page says the dog and cat volunteer opportunities are currently full.

what_you_do: Assist a Teaching Artist in art classes and camps for kids. You prepare materials. You help with hands-on art-making. You act as a role model. It includes an orientation and mentoring.
deadline_text: Winter After-School Class: apply by Dec 29, 2026 (confirmations Jan 5, 2027). Spring Camp: apply by Mar 15, 2027 (confirmations Mar 22, 2027).

what_you_do: You help run Nature Adventures summer camps for young children. The camps are at the Museum and Sea Center. You do crafts, exhibit visits and activities. You earn community service hours. You also learn to teach.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. CIT training was June 12, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

what_you_do: This is a three-to-four year program for high school teens. It has museum studies classes and learning from scientists. It includes camping, field trips and volunteering. After 60 community service hours, you become a paid Museum employee.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications were due April 3, 2026, with in-person interviews in April and orientation week June 21-27, 2026. The page says applications for 2026 opened Feb 1, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You help guests at interpretive tables and science games. You work in the Museum's Backyard, Butterfly Pavilion or Observatory. Shifts are on summer weekends. You earn community service hours.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. Training was May 16-17, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You help summer camp counselors with daily activities. You earn volunteer service hours. You build leadership skills.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. Use the Register link or call Parks and Recreation at 805-564-5418.

what_you_do: These are seasonal and part-time jobs. They help build workplace skills and experience. Titles include Lifeguard, Camp Counselor, Recreation Leader and Seasonal Program Staff.
deadline_text: Aquatics hires year-round; summer hiring is announced in the spring (March 2025 release: tryouts and interviews in April, training before June).

what_you_do: Meet local employers and nonprofits face to face. Look for summer jobs, internships and volunteer roles. A teen interview skills workshop is held the following week.
deadline_text: 2026 fair: Wednesday, April 15, 2026, 4:00 to 6:00 PM at Central Library (workshop April 22). The 2027 date is not posted; the library calls it annual.

what_you_do: You earn community service hours at the library. You can join Teen Volunteer Time. You can join the Teen Advisory Board to plan teen programs and shape the collection. You can also write book reviews.
deadline_text: Teen Advisory Board applications are taken at the start of each school term. Teen Volunteer Time and book reviews are ongoing.

what_you_do: You learn robotics and coding. Then you work in pairs. You plan and lead one robotics program for children. You plan and lead one for teens at the library. There are six programs in all.
deadline_text: Apply by Saturday, October 24, 2026.

what_you_do: You take real college courses while in high school. Santa Barbara and Carpinteria Unified students can take them at their high school. All high school and home school students can take them on the SBCC campus or online.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 dual enrollment registration began July 1. Deadlines for each term are on the Dual Enrollment calendar on the SBCC page.

what_you_do: Help guests at the Stearns Wharf aquarium meet live animals, from sea anemones to small sharks. You do hands-on demos and live animal talks. Teens 14 and up can train as aquarist volunteers.
deadline_text: The Museum's teen page says the Sea Center accepts volunteer applications year-round.

what_you_do: You do a college-level research project. A mentor helps you. The mentor can be a grad student, a postdoc or a faculty member. You go to a research talk series. You take part in university life for about seven weeks.
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 8, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.

what_you_do: You pick a research track in STEM, humanities or social sciences. You take a 4-unit university course. You build a research topic with an instructor. At the end, you present your findings at a capstone seminar.
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 22, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.

what_you_do: Help care for injured and orphaned wildlife at a rescue center, usually one 4-hour shift a week. A parent or guardian volunteers with you.
deadline_text: No dates posted. A mandatory orientation is required.

what_you_do: Speak for teens to City Council and city departments, recommend youth programs and policies, and plan teen events. Meets twice a month.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 City advisory group recruitment: applications due Monday, October 19, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Applications are accepted year-round for future rounds.

what_you_do: These are entry-level seasonal jobs. Examples are Guest Experience Specialist and Zoo Camp positions. The Zoo says most openings are for applicants 14 and older. It welcomes first-time workers for entry-level roles.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The Zoo says the busiest hiring is a month before spring and summer school breaks.

what_you_do: You help run Zoo Camp. You can be a Junior Camp Counselor or a Leader in Training. Or join the Teen Conservation Club. It has monthly meetings and conservation projects.
deadline_text: No application dates are posted. The Zoo volunteer page says it is not taking new volunteer recruitment applications at this time (that line sits in the adult sign-up steps), yet the teen sections still show application links. The Leader in Training dates (June 17 to Aug 23) have no year.

what_you_do: You take a weekend emergency response course. It covers fire safety, search and rescue, stop the bleed and disaster psychology. After it, you can help your community in disasters. You can earn 20+ volunteer hours.
deadline_text: Join the waitlist for the next academy. The site shows January 8 to 10 with no year printed. The last academy was March 13 to 15, 2026.

what_you_do: You advise the City Council on issues that affect teens and help plan events like a 5K run. Fifteen teens serve, and the group meets monthly during the school year.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 recruitment is closed. The page does not give 2027-28 dates.

what_you_do: Teens give input to the library, meet other teens and can earn service hours. Meetings run September through May.
deadline_text: New members are always welcome. No deadline.

what_you_do: Share your views on schools with the County Superintendent at meetings through the school year. You can present at County Board of Education meetings and go on school visits.
deadline_text: The page links a sign-up form but lists no dates or deadline.

what_you_do: Take a weekly job readiness class on resumes, money, networking and interviews, with a career coach. Finish it and you can apply for a paid internship.
deadline_text: Training sessions run Fall (Sept to Nov), Spring (Feb to Apr) and Summer (May to June). The page says the internship application is closed right now.

what_you_do: For about five months you write or direct a short film with a college partner. The 10 films premiere at the historic Arlington Theatre during the festival. You study script writing, casting, cinematography, lighting, sound and editing.
deadline_text: Applications are closed now. The page says the 2027-28 round opens in spring. No deadline posted.

what_you_do: You get an eight week paid county internship, plus job-readiness workshops, hiring events and coaching from an Employment Counselor. You work up to 30 hours a week.
deadline_text: Posted 2026 cohorts: Summer deadline May 20, program June 29 to Aug 7. Fall deadline Sept 19, program Oct 19 to Dec 11. The page also says it is accepting applications now; call to ask about the next cohort. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Teens 14 and older can volunteer at the Santa Clara County Library District. One job is tutoring a student after school. The student is in kindergarten through grade 6.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.

what_you_do: High school students can work as paid student interns in county departments. They help professional staff. They work under close supervision. Tasks depend on the department.
deadline_text: No current posting for Level I. Subscribe to email alerts on the Student Intern, Level I job title or contact county departments. Applications are reviewed as departments ask and expire after 6 months.

what_you_do: Teens tutor students in kindergarten to grade 6. They help with homework after school at a library. You can earn community service hours.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.

what_you_do: This is a non-voting seat on the Library Board. You give feedback on teen programs. You speak for teens at Schaumburg, Conant and Hoffman Estates High Schools. You attend monthly Board meetings. You help with at least two library events.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 term closed Aug 9, 2026. A new application period is likely in summer 2027 but has not been posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the library over the summer. High school students can earn service hours. The library also keeps a list of volunteer options in the community.
deadline_text: The page says opportunities are posted in the spring and take place over the summer. No dates are given for 2027.

what_you_do: Work summer jobs at district pools and The Water Works as a lifeguard, swim instructor or concession worker. Paid lifeguard CPR and AED training is provided. Other seasonal park and recreation jobs are on the district job board.
deadline_text: An aquatics job fair post dated February 18, 2025 listed fairs on Wednesday, March 19; Wednesday, April 16; and Thursday, May 8 at the Community Recreation Center, 505 N. Springinsguth Road. The fair dates have no year printed. 2027 dates are not posted yet. The district job board has live postings.

what_you_do: Through the Sacramento County Office of Education, you can take career technical education courses in 15 industry sectors. The courses mix technical training with academics. The course catalog is posted online.
deadline_text: Course catalog online; no student deadline posted on the page.

what_you_do: Volunteer at a Scripps hospital in a regular weekly shift. You help patients and visitors. Open to teens 15 and older.
deadline_text: South region (Scripps Mercy San Diego and Chula Vista): reviewed on an ongoing basis. North region (Scripps Memorial La Jolla and Encinitas, Scripps Green): applications open the first business day of April (May orientation) and of October (November orientation); applications sent outside those periods are not reviewed.

what_you_do: You staff the hospital information desks or the volunteer office for your first 100 hours. Then you move to an area you like. After 6 months and 100 hours you can ask about shadowing.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are accepted online year-round, and the office is looking for weekday morning or afternoon shifts.

what_you_do: Work with museum staff and other teens to share ideas, shape community programs and plan a hands-on art-making workshop. Meets monthly.
deadline_text: 2026-2027 application closed Oct 1, 2026 and the first meeting is Oct 14, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted; expect a similar fall cycle.

what_you_do: A 40 hour paid training in building jobs for students with disabilities. ANEW runs it with a state job help office. Students earn a certificate.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. The 2026 application deadline was April 30, with notice in early June. No 2027 dates are posted.

what_you_do: Teen volunteers teach visitors about marine life and ocean protection. They join projects like beach cleanups and community science. They get behind-the-scenes tours. They get about 20 hours of training.
deadline_text: School Year 2026-27 Currents interest form is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the Summer 2027 interest form (its general timeline says January; confirm with the Aquarium). Info sessions run over Zoom in March (summer) and September (school year).

what_you_do: Teens get job skills workshops on resumes, interviews and money. Then they get paid internships with local employers. TeamWork Internships are paid game day jobs at Mariners, Kraken and Seahawks games.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page has an Apply button for TeamWork internships and a resume help form.

what_you_do: Free sessions where high school students study one science, such as ancient plants or fish. Teens tour behind the scenes at the Burke collections. They speak at a public STEAM Spotlight Symposium.
deadline_text: Applications for the spring 2026 session are closed. Future dates are not posted; the Burke asks teens to join its Youth and Family Programs e-newsletter.

what_you_do: Weekly volunteer shifts at the hospital and regional clinics. Roles vary; see the position summaries on the volunteer site.
deadline_text: Applications open each March, July and November and stay open until positions are filled. The site lists the next open date (not read).

what_you_do: Four weeks of hands-on biology lab training in downtown Seattle. Teens learn lab skills like PCR and gene editing. They join workshops on college and careers. They present a project of their own.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed March 8, 2026 (letters due March 29). The page says to check back in late 2026 for summer 2027.

what_you_do: Paid training in how research works, then teens consult with Seattle Children's research teams. They give feedback on study plans and outreach and help share results in youth-friendly ways.
deadline_text: No application cycle for 2026-27. The next cycle is 2027-28 and dates are not posted. (The 2025-26 deadline was Sept 1, 2025.)

what_you_do: Learn about clean water, teach students, interview people who work in environmental jobs, and give a final presentation. Field trips and workshops are part of it.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran April 1 to 22, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Train on Saturdays at the fire department training facility to learn what firefighting is like. You get a helmet, coat, pants, boots and gloves for training.
deadline_text: Applications accepted all year. Apply Feb 1 to July 31 and hear back in August. Apply Aug 1 to Jan 31 and hear back in February.

what_you_do: This is eight weeks of paid, full-time lab work. The first two weeks teach lab safety and technique. Then you spend six weeks in a Fred Hutch research group. You go to seminars and college and career workshops. You end with a presentation.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says information on the 2027 program will be posted in November 2026.

what_you_do: A weekly group of teens. They go behind the scenes at the museum and meet artists and creative workers. They make projects like zines, art shows and videos.
deadline_text: Dates for this year are not posted on the pages read. The only call for applications found was for 2023-24 (deadline Oct 10, 2023), so check the Henry teen page.

what_you_do: A two week summer program at the history museum. Teens learn how to research and tell local history. Then they publish their own project on the Rainy Day History website.
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was May 22, 2026 and has passed. The page says to check back in spring 2027.

what_you_do: Teen volunteers help visitors at the air and space museum. Roles include guiding tours, helping with school trips, and acting out history with costumes and props. Open roles are listed on the page.
deadline_text: Roles are recruited by season. No single deadline. Browse current roles and apply online.

what_you_do: Teens do a 4 Saturday job training and mentor program. Then they can apply for a paid summer internship with Seattle Parks. Interns work 20 hours a week for 8 weeks, for example on summer meals and playgrounds.
deadline_text: Page says mentorship applications opened in August 2026. Mentorship starts the first Saturday of October, November, February, March and April. No close date stated.

what_you_do: You watch swimmers. You respond to emergencies. You help teach swim skills. This is at city swim beaches and indoor and outdoor pools.
deadline_text: The last posting closed June 16, 2026. The Aquatics page says Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round, even when no posting is active.

what_you_do: Work a city summer job such as wading pool attendant, aquatics customer service, boat ramp ranger or lifeguard. Some jobs are mostly weekends and some include first aid training.
deadline_text: 2026 postings closed between May 12 and June 16, 2026 (page updated April 14, 2026). 2027 postings not posted.

what_you_do: Interns help run Late Night teen events at Seattle teen life centers and community centers. They check teens in. They help with games, contests, community dinners and service projects.
deadline_text: Applications for the January to June cohort open in December. Applications for the June to December cohort open in May. Exact close dates are not stated.

what_you_do: A summer theater program where youth rehearse and perform a full musical (Peter Pan in 2026). The program is aimed at youth of color. Rehearsals ran June 29 to Aug 27 in 2026, with shows Aug 28 to 30.
deadline_text: 2026 auditions were April 17 and 18. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A 7-week, 14-hour after-school job readiness class (resume writing, time management, professional communication) at Teen Life Centers or community centers. Finishing it unlocks Parks paid internships.
deadline_text: Offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter. The page does not list current dates, so email to ask.

what_you_do: Learn how police work through monthly meetings and visits to units like K-9 and Harbor Patrol. Volunteer at community events, such as directing traffic and security work. Uniforms are provided.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Explorers meet monthly.

what_you_do: Lead the planning of Girlvolution, a youth arts and social justice event, with training, a mentor and a $5,000 event budget. Also help run 3 other community events.
deadline_text: Applications closed for 2026. The page says to check back next year. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Support peers, help build a healing justice curriculum and help plan the Healing Justice Summit. You work with a team of staff, mental health providers and community partners.
deadline_text: Applications closed for 2026. The page says to check back next year. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer in a hospital with training for your role. You do about 48 hours over roughly 3 months with at least one 3 to 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: No application dates are listed. The page says to apply through the online form.

what_you_do: Spend half your school day in a hands-on career class such as aerospace manufacturing, dental assisting, certified nursing assistant, video game programming, auto, construction or cyber security. 21 programs.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 lottery has run and all offers have been made. The admissions page asks students still interested in 2026-27 to complete the PSSC Application interest form. The 2027-28 window is not posted.

what_you_do: A 6-week paid summer internship for 20 teens. Interns explore career paths, take field trips, hear guest speakers and work on personal growth.
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened in April 2026. Close date not stated. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Visit transportation sites, meet people in planning, engineering and communications, job shadow, and build resume and interview skills. Learn about advocacy for fair transportation.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed June 16, 2026. Program ran Aug 4 to 27, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Work part time at a local nonprofit for the summer. TIPS hires you and places you based on your interests, such as a camp, an arts group or a food bank.
deadline_text: Applications open mid to late November 2026 (exact day not posted). Deadline Feb 5, 2027. Interviews early to mid March, decisions April 2027.

what_you_do: A cohort of teens works with TeenTix and Seattle arts groups. They learn about arts careers, give feedback from the teen view, lead skill-shares and act as a teen council.
deadline_text: The page does not state application dates or whether applications are open. Check the TeenTix Program Applications page.

what_you_do: Teen writers see arts events for free and write reviews that are edited by teen editors and posted on the TeenTix blog. Some work is also shared with Encore and The Seattle Times.
deadline_text: The page does not give application dates or say whether applications are open. It refers to the 2026-2027 season. Check the TeenTix Program Applications page.

what_you_do: This in-person summer program runs four weeks at UW Seattle. You learn coding through projects. You explore how technology affects society. You work in groups led by UW undergraduate mentors.
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: applications opened March 4 and closed April 1, 2026 (11:59pm PT); decisions April 27; orientation May 16. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A free one week summer program at UW Seattle for teens new to engineering. Students do hands-on design tasks, meet engineering students and teachers, and tour campus.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The page says the 2027 application will open in March.

what_you_do: This is a two-week summer program on the UW Seattle campus. It has leadership workshops. You join a real-world business case competition. You visit two Seattle companies.
deadline_text: No deadline stated; 'spaces are limited.' The only session listed was July 5 to 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: A week long day camp. You shadow nurses at two UW hospitals, learn CPR and how to take vital signs, practice in simulation labs and meet nurses from different fields.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran July 20 to 24, 2026. Applications for 2027 open February 15, 2027. Closing date not stated.

what_you_do: High school students take regular UW summer courses for college credit. More than 1,000 courses are offered on campus and online.
deadline_text: The page gives 2026 steps (eighth grade completed by June 30, 2026; summer began June 22, 2026). Its calendar lists February 2027 as when the Time Schedule and application open for 2027, with no exact date.

what_you_do: Take tuition-free, year-long career classes in 3 hour blocks while still in high school. Many give high school and college credit or an industry certification. A summer semester is also offered.
deadline_text: The full-year priority window ran Feb 4, 2026 to March 31, 2026. Full-year applications closed July 15 (the year is not printed on that line). Summer 2027 information is not posted yet.

what_you_do: A free after-school arts program. Teens work with teaching artists on art about identity and culture, learn about arts careers, and show their work in the museum's youth gallery.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page says registration typically opens in the spring and is first come, first served. Email the museum to ask about info sessions.

what_you_do: You meet each week to learn about conservation careers, public speaking and teamwork. You also pick your own volunteer shifts at the zoo. There are 20 shifts. They can include Zoomazium, new habitats and animal behavior observation.
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: application deadline Friday, March 27, 2026, 5:00 pm; Q&A sessions in March; interviews mid-April; decisions early May. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Join a youth-led environmental club at your school or start one. Take part in monthly service projects, a leaders summit, spring retreats and a spring environmental symposium.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Events: Environmental Leaders Summit (the page says both winter and each fall), Eco-Retreats and Environmental Symposium (spring).

what_you_do: Be a role model and lead campers in grades 1 to 8 through crafts, STEM, archery, hikes and outdoor games at a local YMCA summer day camp.
deadline_text: Page says "Now hiring for summer". No application window posted for summer 2027. Training for some jobs starts in May or June.

what_you_do: Explore a career path and get paid to learn job and life skills. The program is run with Thompson Hotels and Machinists INC and funded by the City of Seattle.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page appears out of date (it mentions a 2025 event), so ask about the next cohort.

what_you_do: Join a weekly delegation, write your own bill, then debate and vote on student bills as a mock legislator at the State Capitol conference in Olympia.
deadline_text: Delegations start meeting Oct 19, 2026 (some later, up to Nov 4). Open houses are listed for Oct 8 and Oct 14 (the page prints no year for them). No sign-up deadline stated.

what_you_do: Fifteen teens are picked by the Mayor and City Council. They advise the City on rules that affect youth. They plan a community project and a yearly event. They learn public speaking and how to organize.
deadline_text: Applications are paused. Email the commission to be told when it reopens. No dates posted.

what_you_do: These are paid summer internships. They are in City departments, local businesses and nonprofits. They run July 6 to Aug 18 in 2026. There is also a school-year Learn & Earn job skills program with stipends.
deadline_text: 2026 internship applications ran March 18 to May 5, 2026 (closed). Learn & Earn Foundations 2026-27 applications ran Aug 11 to Sept 25, 2026 (closed). 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Learn photography and design, work on real projects for paying clients, build a portfolio and practice job interviews. Meets twice a week at the Youth in Focus office.
deadline_text: 2027 application "opens soon". Exact dates are not set on the page. The page lists the 2027 steps as a November deadline (a Sunday, date not set), interviews in December and a January start.

what_you_do: Get paid to photograph events for local groups and businesses, with a teaching artist mentoring you. Youth in Focus provides all the camera equipment.
deadline_text: No deadline. Take a class first, then ask about jobs.

what_you_do: You can get free after-school writing help, workshops, summer programs, and college and leadership support. SFPL lists leadership and writing roles for grades 8 to 12 that pay a stipend.
deadline_text: No dates posted. Check the 826 Valencia program calendar.

what_you_do: High school students are role models for middle schoolers. This is a summer program. You co-teach an elective like dance or soccer. You help with after-school tutoring. You lead cheers and plan events.
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says the summer 2027 application launches in early 2027; exact dates not posted.

what_you_do: You do a paid, year-round internship that lasts 2 to 3 years. You do fieldwork, teach visitors and join research projects after school and on Saturdays.
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027; closing date not posted.

what_you_do: Take free City College classes while in high school and earn both high school and college credit.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page. Ask your counselor before each term.

what_you_do: You can attend this one-day job fair. You meet employers, learn about openings, get resume help, practice interviews, take headshots and get free professional clothing.
deadline_text: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 12:00 to 4:00 p.m. at Stonestown Galleria.

what_you_do: Learn how to plan and run pre-registration events that help 16 and 17 year olds sign up to vote. Includes an in-person training and a mentor from the Department of Elections.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed (the round ran Sept 14 to 27, 2026). The program runs twice a year, in April and September. Spring 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You do a paid museum job. You help visitors at exhibits, lead demonstrations such as cow's eye dissections, and help run museum operations. You get more than 60 hours of training.
deadline_text: School-year applications are typically posted in July and summer applications in March. Closing dates are not stated.

what_you_do: This is a free Saturday program. It teaches basic firefighting, CPR and first aid. It also teaches life skills, such as money skills, leadership and time management.
deadline_text: Not stated on the academy's site. A 2025 news article reported an Aug 11, 2025 deadline for the fall class.

what_you_do: You coach elementary and middle school girls. The program covers running and life skills. You are a junior coach. You work 1.5 to 3 hours a week for 8 to 10 weeks.
deadline_text: The fall 2026 Junior Coach application was due Aug 26, 2026 (season started early September; 5K on Nov 14, 2026). Spring dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You can take free semester-long coding classes. You can take computer science classes too. Classes are in person or remote. There are also workshops, self-paced courses and events.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 class registration is closed. Spring 2027 classes are not posted yet. Workshops and events are posted separately (College Connections is Nov 7, 2026).

what_you_do: If you are a younger teen, you get job readiness training. You get paid work experience. You also get homework help and mentoring.
deadline_text: School-year round closed Sept 14, 2026. The YMCA page says summer applications are due the first week of April; school-year applications the first week of September.

what_you_do: You can get a six month paid internship with employer partners, plus job coaching, if you are out of school or work.
deadline_text: Applications accepted all year (per the sf.gov youth listing).

what_you_do: You can get a paid summer internship with local organizations and businesses, plus career workshops and mentorship. Black 2 San Francisco is a separate 6 week program for 30 students.
deadline_text: The 2026 OFA deadline was April 10, 2026. The summer application is closed; 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Sign up early so you are on the voter list the day you turn 18. Pairs well with the SF elections ambassador program.
deadline_text: Always open.

what_you_do: You can get a paid summer internship in City departments, with a focus on public service and careers such as architecture, business, engineering and science.
deadline_text: The 2027 timeline on the application page says 'details coming soon'. Dates are not posted.

what_you_do: You get your first job at rec centers and parks. Areas include arts, sports, aquatics, gardening and cooking. Facility operations is another area.
deadline_text: No dates posted. Email the program to ask when the next round opens.

what_you_do: Help with children's and family programs at branch libraries. Openings listed include Ingleside, Noe Valley and North Beach (Cantonese or Mandarin speakers).
deadline_text: Rolling. Some positions start late October or early November 2026.

what_you_do: This is a paid summer internship. You work at the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission or at a private engineering firm. The firm works on the sewer system. The program is for students from southeast San Francisco neighborhoods.
deadline_text: No dates posted on the SFPUC page.

what_you_do: You can volunteer at the SF Zoo in three teen programs. Nature Trail is for ages 12 to 14. You show small animals to guests. Junior Zoologists is for ages 15 to 17. You help with animal care. Leadership Fellows is for grades 10 to 12. You help run Zoo Camp.
deadline_text: Nature Trail applications open each March (the page says 2027 applications open in March). Junior Zoologists and Leadership Fellows were closed on the pages read; 2026 Leadership Fellows group interviews were Apr 25, 2026. No 2027 closing dates posted.

what_you_do: You can attend a free summer camp at UCSF's Parnassus campus. It has lectures, games and Q&A sessions. It has patient panels and live anatomy dissections. UCSF students and faculty mentor you.
deadline_text: The page is out of date (titled Summer Camp 2025, it says 2026 applications are open but posts no dates), so email the program through the Contact Us link before applying.

what_you_do: You do a paid eight-week summer research internship at UCSF with a scientist mentor. The program also includes college counseling and a trip to a college campus.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. Last cycle's deadline was Sunday, Feb 8 (the 2026 application). 2027 dates are not posted; fill in the page's interest form to be notified.

what_you_do: You can join free after-school art programs for public high school students. Professional artists lead them, and they build creative, technical and leadership skills.
deadline_text: Contact YAX for current sessions.

what_you_do: You can do paid job readiness workshops. You can do internships in City departments, such as the Public Library and SFO Airport. The program also offers mentoring and college tours.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 school-year application is closed (the DCYF newsletter listed Sept 14, 2026). The Youth Leadership Team application is marked coming soon. Summer dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Volunteer in the hospital for at least one year, with one 2 to 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: Application window Oct 1 to Nov 13, 2026 (per the program page). Application packet due 6 p.m. Nov 12, 2026. Teacher evaluation due Dec 11, 2026. Results by email Jan 31, 2027.

what_you_do: High school students can take SJSU summer college courses for credit. They do not have to be admitted first. They take them through Open University. There are more than 500 courses.
deadline_text: Summer 2026: Open University registration began April 15 and closed July 13. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You can join a career and technical education club at school. It offers skills contests. It offers leadership training. It connects you to employers.
deadline_text: Join through your CTE teacher. No cycle stated.

what_you_do: Teens go to trainings and workshops. They support some public programs at the Skirball. They help with research for the remodel of the permanent collection. Members also get into Skirball events for free.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are closed. The next window is not posted.

what_you_do: Join teen service events during the school year and school breaks. The Teen Library Council meets regularly on Thursday afternoons.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: You can compete on a high school team in a science and math quiz at SLAC. Winning teams can move on to the national event, and volunteers are also needed.
deadline_text: Registration opened Oct 5, 2026. High school event is Feb 27, 2027 (middle school is Feb 6, 2027). Registration deadline not posted.

what_you_do: You can attend a free one-week science camp for high schoolers from all backgrounds. It has hands-on science on the SLAC and Stanford campuses.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 24 to Mar 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: This is a free STEM program. STEM means science, technology, engineering and math. You live at a university partner for the summer, such as UC Berkeley. It includes computer science, college success, elective classes and STEM career mentors.
deadline_text: Application dates for 2026 to 27 are not posted. Join the interest list for updates.

what_you_do: You can take tuition-free college classes through your high school and earn high school and college credit at the same time.
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask your counselor about each term.

what_you_do: You do a paid six-week summer internship in areas such as IT, engineering, customer service, vehicle mechanics, accounting, HR and marketing.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Mar 23, 2026 and closed May 1, 2026 (5 pm). 2027 dates not posted yet.

what_you_do: Free job training, work experience and internships. You also get skill training and help finding a job. STEP gives work experience for your resume and applications.
deadline_text: No deadlines listed. A Youth Job Fair is linked but no date is on the page.

what_you_do: Spend two weeks in a residential program on a college campus. You work on SAT prep and career growth. You also work on resume writing, college applications and admission, and leadership.
deadline_text: Applications open Jan 29, 2027 and close Mar 29, 2027. No late submissions accepted.

what_you_do: Take one real college course for four weeks on campus: English 101, Biology 100 or Dance 132. You earn four college credits with a grade of C or better.
deadline_text: Applications open Jan 29, 2027 and close Mar 29, 2027. No late submissions accepted.

what_you_do: Volunteer at the library during the school year or in a summer session. The application also asks whether you can work on your own and if you have a driver's license.
deadline_text: No deadline or dates are posted on the application page.

what_you_do: You do mentored, hands-on summer research in health AI. You work with real-world health data on problems where AI and medicine meet.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 program. Application opens Nov 10, 2026 and closes Feb 1, 2027. Free online info session Tue Nov 10, 2026, 5 to 6 pm Pacific, open to students and parents.

what_you_do: This is a two-week in-person summer program. It covers health topics that affect Asian communities. You learn AI basics and leadership skills. You also learn about precision health data.
deadline_text: 2027 dates will be announced in fall 2026. Sign up for announcements.

what_you_do: You can volunteer as a teen in one of five areas: mother and baby care, play and recreation, support services, education, and community-based activities.
deadline_text: Openings and requirements are shown during the online orientation. No dates on the page.

what_you_do: This is an eight-week summer genetics and genomics research project in a Stanford lab. You work 4 hours a day, 5 days a week. That is about 20 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: opened Dec 2025, due Feb 28, 2026 at 11:59pm (fee waiver request due Feb 15). 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You can do non-medical volunteer roles in the hospital, one shift a week for at least six months. It is not shadowing and does not count as clinical hours.
deadline_text: The page says to use the portal to see the next application dates. Dates not shown on the page I read.

what_you_do: You take a two-week hands-on medicine course with skills like ultrasound, dissection and suturing. This is a fee-based program. You pay to attend, and it is not a job.
deadline_text: All 2026 programs closed. The page says the next cycle opens Jan 1, 2027; no 2027 deadline posted. Last cycle: Nov 1, 2025 to Feb 9, 2026.

what_you_do: You do a seven-week summer internship in pediatrics at Stanford, about 30 hours a week. It is for students from nearby counties.
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Feb 23, 2026 (decisions Apr 1, 2026). 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You can take one live online college-style course, Monday to Friday for two weeks, as a middle or high school student. You may take only one course per summer.
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Mar 13, 2026 (decisions mid-May 2026). 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: You do eight weeks of full-time biomedical lab research with Stanford faculty and graduate student mentors. Morning lectures are held at the start.
deadline_text: Application opens Dec 18, 2026 at 5pm Pacific; due late February 2027 (exact date not posted). 2026 deadline was Feb 21, 2026.

what_you_do: You can join a five-week, tuition-free summer program on Stanford's campus to explore medicine. It is for current juniors from low-income and first-generation backgrounds.
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 23, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

what_you_do: Meet one Saturday a month. You meet city leaders and learn how city government works. You also learn about public safety and leadership. You learn about community and economic development. One trip is to the Georgia State Capitol.
deadline_text: The city's Sept. 3, 2026 notice says registration opens that day. No deadline is listed. It closes when all 30 spots are filled. Sessions: Oct 24, Nov 14, Dec 12, 2026; Jan 30, Feb (Capitol date to be set), Mar 20, 2027.

what_you_do: Year-round support for students who would be the first in their family to go to college. You get after-school and summer programs and tutoring. You also get college advice, leadership building and career exploration. It runs from 6th grade through college.
deadline_text: New student applications open October 20, 2026. Deadline is in January 2027 (no day stated). Information session in December.

what_you_do: Shelve books, help with grounds care, help at the summer reading check-in table, or do a short service hour project. The library has a VolunTEENs program just for ages 13 to 18.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Summer reading volunteering is seasonal.

what_you_do: This is a free, live in leadership academy for teens who are behind in school. Cadets work on discipline, life skills and school credits. The site says up to 65 high school credits. There is support for 12 months after graduation.
deadline_text: Class 39 begins in January 2027. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. The next in person orientation is October 24, 2026 at 1 PM at 4022 Saratoga Ave, Bldg 21, Los Alamitos. A Final Roll Call is held in December; without a finished application and roll call you will not be considered for Class 39.

what_you_do: Youth 13 and older can volunteer. They can help at special events or do office tasks. They can also work with young people or seniors. Library roles are included.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Roles are posted as needed.

what_you_do: Help staff run sport, art, dance, drama, science and themed day camps and youth programs at Surrey rec centres.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page read. Check for the next intake.

what_you_do: Twenty Surrey teens meet every other week at City Hall. They give the city a youth voice. They plan the Youth Speak Up Forum and the Surrey Leadership Action Conference.
deadline_text: Applications for this term are closed. The city says they reopen in Spring 2027.

what_you_do: Read with a child in grades 2 to 4 for one hour a week for six weeks and do fun reading activities. You are the 'Big Buddy'.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 teen applications closed. Fall sessions run Oct 13 to Nov 25, 2026. Spring sessions are expected next.

what_you_do: Teen ambassadors for the library plan events. They tell the library what services teens want. Six councils meet at branches around Surrey.
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page gives no reopening date.

what_you_do: Help with information, giving directions and office tasks. You also support patients. Some units need volunteers who are 20 or older.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are kept on file for four months.

what_you_do: Pitch a youth-led project for Surrey, like an event, public art or a workshop. Funding may be available but is not guaranteed.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

what_you_do: Work with city staff to plan youth events like Surrey Slam Jam, the Youth Cooking Showdown and the Kids Conference. You also help run them on the day.
deadline_text: Applications for this term are closed. The city says they reopen in Spring 2027.

what_you_do: Drop-in park work with other teens: pull invasive plants, plant trees and shrubs, clean up litter and improve habitat. Tools and training are provided.
deadline_text: Drop-in dates: Sep 25, Oct 23 and Nov 14, 2026. More dates go to registered members.

what_you_do: High school job-skills classes in 22 career tracks, including AI engineering, auto repair, culinary arts, nursing, heating and cooling (HVAC), animation and fire science. Some give college credit, and some prepare you for an apprenticeship (paid job training).
deadline_text: Not stated on the pages read. Ask your counselor for enrollment dates.

what_you_do: Drop-in teen groups that plan library programs, give feedback and do service projects. Teens earn volunteer hours and build leadership skills. There is also a virtual council.
deadline_text: Runs October through April. No application, so you can join any time during the season.

what_you_do: A six-week summer service-learning program. A cohort of teens meets weekly and works on service projects to build resume skills.
deadline_text: Applications typically open in April and are posted on the teen volunteering page. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Internships with Tacoma businesses and groups. Students apply in SchooLinks and interview with employers. They finish their hours and tasks. They earn school credit and a stipend.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 sessions are: Session 1 Sept 9 to Nov 19 (applications open in August); Session 2 Nov 30 to Feb 4 (applications open in October); Session 3 Feb 17 to Apr 15 (January); Session 4 Apr 26 to June 17 (March); Session 5 July 6 to Aug 20 (May). The page does not say whether applications are open today.

what_you_do: Free summer training from experts. The 2026 page lists courses in cars, cooking, digital drawing, business starts, plumbing, building, drones and wildland fire. Students earn credentials.
deadline_text: The auto course priority deadline was April 30. 2027 dates are not posted.

what_you_do: Take college and career courses at a technical college while in high school and earn high school and college credit at the same time. Funding covers tuition, fees and books for the first 30 hours.
deadline_text: Each college sets deadlines. Atlanta Technical College lists June 1 for fall, Nov 1 for spring and April 1 for summer (no year stated).

what_you_do: Teen volunteers lead hands-on science, tech and art activities for museum visitors. This is during the holiday season. Volunteers complete six shifts. Each shift is 3 to 4 hours.
deadline_text: The official page gives no application dates as of Oct 9, 2026.

what_you_do: Teens train to give peer support to other teens by hotline, text and email. Adult mental health pros guide the work.
deadline_text: The page says applications are due "Monday September 8, 2026 by 5pm" (that date is a Tuesday, so confirm the day), which has now passed. Training runs three times a year (Fall, Spring, Summer). Next dates are not posted; the page has an email interest list for future applications.

what_you_do: Help shape what the library offers for teens and earn community service hours.
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due no later than August 21, 2026. Next year's date is not posted.

what_you_do: Join a county 4-H club and pick at least one project. Take part in club meetings, events and contests. The program offers hands-on leadership, community service and career discovery.
deadline_text: Enroll by October 31 for the lower fee ($25). After that the fee is $30 until the end of the 4-H year. Memberships reset every August 15.

what_you_do: Spend a week running a pretend city, county and state government. You join one of two practice political parties, run for office, hear speakers and debate.
deadline_text: 2027 dates and the application deadline are not posted on the pages read. The 2026 session ran June 7 to 12, 2026. The site shows an Applications Now Open banner, but it posts no deadline or 2027 dates, so ask your school and local Post.
